definition_zh: 半球；地球半球；大脑半球；半球图；（活动）范围
definition_en: one half of a sphere, especially the northern or southern half of the earth
core_image: 一个球被过球心的大圆切成两半，每一半都保留着完整的弧面
scene: 地理老师在球体模型上沿赤道画了一圈。The teacher cuts the globe along the equator to show each hemisphere.
sceneCN: 这里 hemisphere 指「地球被赤道分成的南北两半之一」（第 1 个义项：以赤道为界划分的地球半球）；句意为老师沿赤道切开地球仪，展示南北两个半球。图中可辨识物件：地球仪、赤道线、半圆剖面、支架。

senses.title: Half of the earth
senses.titleCN: 地球的半球：以赤道或经圈分成的两半
senses.definition: either the northern or southern half of the earth, divided by the equator, or the eastern and western halves divided by meridians
senses.definitionCN: 地球被赤道分成南北两半，或被经线分成东西两半的任一半
senses.example: Most of the world's population lives in the northern hemisphere.
senses.exampleCN: 世界人口大部分住在北半球。
senses.why: Hemi- 'half' plus sphaira 'sphere' literally gives 'half ball'; once applied to the earth, it names each of its two halves.
senses.whyCN: hemi-「一半」加 sphaira「球」字面就是「半个球」；用于地球后，就指地球的两半之一。

senses.title: Half of any sphere
senses.titleCN: 半球体：任意球体被大圆切开的一半
senses.definition: one of the two halves of a sphere cut by a plane through its centre
senses.definitionCN: 球体被过球心平面切开后的任一半
senses.example: A hemisphere has a curved surface and one flat circular face.
senses.exampleCN: 半球有一个曲面和一个平的圆面。
senses.why: The geometry sense is the literal one: a sphere divided by a great circle leaves two equal halves.
senses.whyCN: 几何义是字面义：球被大圆分割，留下两个相等的半。

senses.title: One side of the brain
senses.titleCN: 大脑半球：大脑左右两半之一
senses.definition: either of the two halves of the brain, left and right, divided by the central fissure
senses.definitionCN: 大脑被中央沟分成左右两半的任一半
senses.example: The left hemisphere usually handles language in right-handed people.
senses.exampleCN: 惯用右手的人通常由左半球处理语言。
senses.why: The brain is roughly spherical, so its two lobes were named hemispheres when anatomy borrowed the word.
senses.whyCN: 大脑近似球形，解剖学借这个词时就把左右两叶称作半球。

senses.title: A map of one half of the globe
senses.titleCN: 半球图：展示地球一半的地图
senses.definition: a map projection that shows one half of the globe at a time
senses.definitionCN: 一次展示地球一半的地图投影
senses.example: The atlas opens with a hemisphere map of the Pacific.
senses.exampleCN: 这本图集以一幅太平洋半球图开篇。
senses.why: A flat map can show only half the globe without severe distortion, so such maps are called hemisphere maps.
senses.whyCN: 平面地图不严重变形时只能展示地球一半，这类图因而叫半球图。

senses.title: Eastern or western division
senses.titleCN: 东西半球：按经度划分的政治地理分区
senses.definition: either of the two east-west divisions of the globe, often used as a cultural or political label
senses.definitionCN: 地球按经度划分的东西两半，常用作文化或政治标签
senses.example: The convention placed the new nation in the western hemisphere.
senses.exampleCN: 这一惯例把新国家归入西半球。
senses.why: Meridians can split the globe into two named halves just as the equator does, and those names then acquire cultural and political weight.
senses.whyCN: 经线也能像赤道一样把地球分成两个有名称的半，而这些名称随后带上文化与政治分量。

senses.title: Half of the celestial sphere
senses.titleCN: 天球半球：天球被地平圈分成的一半
senses.definition: either half of the sky as divided by the horizon or by a celestial great circle
senses.definitionCN: 天空被地平圈或天球大圆分成的任一半
senses.example: Astronomers chart the visible hemisphere before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家在黎明前绘制可见天球半球。
senses.why: The horizon cuts the spherical sky into a visible half and a hidden half, the same geometry as the globe.
senses.whyCN: 地平圈把球形天空切成可见与不可见两半，与地球的几何分割相同。

senses.title: A sphere of activity or influence
senses.titleCN: 活动范围：影响所及的领域（书面）
senses.definition: an area of activity, knowledge or influence, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 活动、知识或影响所及的范围，用于比喻
senses.example: The reform moved education into a different hemisphere of public debate.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革把教育推入公共讨论的另一个领域。
senses.why: The globe's two halves are imagined as two separate worlds, so any divided field can be called a hemisphere.
senses.whyCN: 地球的两半被想象成两个分开的世界，因此任何被分割的领域都可称为一个 hemisphere。

senses.title: Land or water hemisphere
senses.titleCN: 陆半球或水半球：按海陆分布划分的半球
senses.definition: either of two halves of the earth chosen to contain most of its land or most of its water
senses.definitionCN: 地球按陆地或水域最集中而划分出的两半之一
senses.example: The land hemisphere is centred near southern Europe.
senses.exampleCN: 陆半球以欧洲南部附近为中心。
senses.why: Geographers may choose the centre so that most land falls in one half and most water in the other, which makes the division a deliberate cut.
senses.whyCN: 地理学家可以选择中心，使大部分陆地落在一半、大部分水域落在另一半，因此这种划分是有意选定的切法。

intro.en: Hemisphere goes back to Greek hemisphairion, 'half a sphere', from hemi- 'half' and sphaira 'ball'. Latin took it as hemisphaerium and English borrowed it in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hemisphere 上溯到希腊 hemisphairion「半个球」，由 hemi-「一半」与 sphaira「球」构成；拉丁作 hemisphaerium，英语在 16 世纪借入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Hemi- meant 'half' and is a productive prefix in English, as in hemicycle and hemisphere.
items.cn: hemi- 意为「一半」，在英语中是能产前缀，如 hemicycle 与 hemisphere。

items.en: Sphaira meant 'ball, globe'. Its deeper origin is not established; any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction, not a recorded form.
items.cn: sphaira 意为「球、globus」；其更深来源未得到证明，为其提出的任何印欧词根都属重构形式，而非有记录的词。

items.en: Hemi- plus sphaira gave hemisphairion, 'a half sphere', used by Greek geographers and astronomers.
items.cn: hemi- 加 sphaira 构成 hemisphairion「半球」，为希腊地理学家与天文学家所用。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek compound as hemisphaerium, keeping both elements intact.
items.cn: 拉丁把这个希腊复合词借作 hemisphaerium，两个成分原样保留。

items.en: English hemisphere appears in the sixteenth century, first for the halves of the celestial and terrestrial spheres.
items.cn: 英语 hemisphere 出现于 16 世纪，最初指天球与地球的半球。

items.en: The anatomical use for the two halves of the brain developed later; its exact first English date is uncertain, while the compound itself is transparent.
items.cn: 指大脑两半的解剖用法较晚出现；其英语首见确切年代不确定，但复合词本身结构透明。

note.en: Group one holds the -sphere words that look alike; group two holds words for halves, globes and brain regions.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近的 -sphere 词；第二组是表示一半、球体与脑区的词。

entries.definition: From Greek atmos 'vapour' plus sphaira: the envelope of air around a planet, not a half of it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 atmos「蒸汽」加 sphaira：行星周围的空气层，不是球的一半。

entries.definition: From Greek bios 'life' plus sphaira: the zone of living things, named by analogy with atmosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 bios「生命」加 sphaira：生物所在圈层，仿 atmosphere 造出。

entries.definition: The ionised layer of the upper atmosphere; again a full shell, not a hemisphere.
entries.definitionCN: 高层大气中的电离层；同样是完整壳层而非半球。

entries.definition: From Latin stratum 'layer' plus sphaira: a layer of the atmosphere, with no half division.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 stratum「层」加 sphaira：大气的一层，不含对半分割。

entries.definition: The everyday word for one of two equal parts; hemisphere adds the spherical shape.
entries.definitionCN: 表示两个相等部分之一的日常词；hemisphere 另带球体形状。

entries.definition: The whole spherical earth or a model of it; a hemisphere is only one of its halves.
entries.definitionCN: 整个球形地球或其模型；半球只是它的一半。

entries.definition: A rounded projecting part, as of the brain or lung; hemisphere stresses the left-right division.
entries.definitionCN: 圆形突出的部分，如脑叶或肺叶；hemisphere 强调左右分半。

entries.definition: A band or region defined by climate or function; it cuts the globe into belts rather than halves.
entries.definitionCN: 按气候或功能划分的带或区域；它把地球切成带而非两半。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek compound, real map terms and real anatomy, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊复合词、真实的地图术语与真实的解剖学，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Hemi- 'half' + sphaira 'sphere': literally half a ball, then half the earth.
normal.cn: hemi-「一半」+ sphaira「球」：字面是半个球，再指地球的一半。

normal.en: The -sphere family (atmosphere, biosphere, ionosphere) is built on the same Greek 'ball'.
normal.cn: atmosphere、biosphere、ionosphere 等 -sphere 词族都建立在同一个希腊「球」上。

normal.en: Northern and southern hemispheres are divided by the equator; eastern and western by meridians.
normal.cn: 南北半球由赤道分开，东西半球由经线分开。

normal.en: The brain's two hemispheres are linked by the corpus callosum.
normal.cn: 大脑两个半球由胼胝体相连。

normal.en: A hemisphere map shows half the globe at once, which limits distortion.
normal.cn: 半球图一次展示地球一半，从而限制变形。

abstract.en: Picture an orange sliced exactly through its centre into two equal cups.
abstract.cn: 想象一只橙子沿正中心切成两只相等的杯状半。

abstract.en: Picture a theatre with the audience seated on one side of the stage only.
abstract.cn: 想象一座剧场，观众只坐在舞台的一侧。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation that belongs to one half of a divided family.
abstract.cn: 想象一场只属于分裂家庭中某一方的对话。

examples.en: Summer begins in the southern hemisphere in December.
examples.cn: 南半球的夏天在十二月开始。

examples.en: Each hemisphere of the brain has different functions.
examples.cn: 大脑每个半球各有不同功能。

examples.en: The map folds out into two hemispheres.
examples.cn: 这张地图展开后分成两个半球图。

dict_mnemonic.text: hemi（一半，如 hemi- 前缀）+ sphere（球）→ 半个球 → 半球、大脑半球

root: 希腊 hemisphairion「半球」= hemi-（一半）+ sphaira（球）；拉丁 hemisphaerium，英语 16 世纪借入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin with a sphere and a cut through its centre: the earth's halves, any ball's halves, the brain's two sides, a map of one half, the east-west labels, the sky's halves, a figurative field, and the land-water division.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「球体被过球心切开」开始：地球两半、任意球体的两半、大脑两侧、展示一半的地图、东西半球标签、天空两半、比喻的领域，以及陆半球与水半球。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sphere cut exactly through its centre, leaving two equal curved halves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个球被过球心切开，留下两个相等的弧面半。

branches.en: GEOMETRY TO EARTH: the literal half ball becomes the earth's northern and southern halves.
branches.cn: 几何到地球：字面的半个球变成地球的南北两半。

branches.en: BODY: the brain's two sides borrow the spherical division.
branches.cn: 身体：大脑两侧借用了球体的分割。

branches.en: DRAWN AND CHOSEN: maps show one half at a time, and land or water can define an uneven half.
branches.cn: 画出与选定：地图一次展示一半，陆地或水域也能划出不完全对等的一半。

branches.en: LABEL AND METAPHOR: east-west halves are political names, and any field can be pictured as a half.
branches.cn: 标签与比喻：东西半球是政治名称，任何领域也可被想象成一半。

branches.en: SKY: the celestial sphere is cut by the horizon into visible and invisible halves.
branches.cn: 天空：天球被地平圈分成可见与不可见的两半。

intro.en: Hemisphere joins a Greek prefix for 'half' to the Greek word for 'ball'; the second element also builds the atmosphere and biosphere words.
intro.cn: hemisphere 把希腊「一半」前缀与希腊「球」词连在一起；后一成分还构成 atmosphere 与 biosphere 等词。

latinIntro.en: Greek sphaira 'ball' passed into Latin as sphaera and into English as -sphere; hemi- remains a live prefix in English compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 sphaira「球」传入拉丁作 sphaera，再进入英语作 -sphere；hemi- 在英语复合词中仍是能产前缀。

items.example: The prefix cuts the sphere exactly in two.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把球正好切成两半。

items.example: The root supplies the round shape.
The northern hemisphere is warmer in July.
Hemispheric trade grew after the treaty.
items.exampleCN: 条约签订后半球间贸易增长。

items.example: The child recovered after a hemispherectomy.
items.exampleCN: 这个孩子在半球切除术后康复。

items.example: The biosphere extends through land and sea.
items.exampleCN: 生物圈遍及陆地与海洋。

items.example: Radio signals bounce off the ionosphere.
items.exampleCN: 无线电信号从电离层反射。

definition_en: for this reason, or from this time
core_image: 从这一点出发，射出的一条因果线
scene: 路上结了冰，因此他们决定待在家里。The roads were icy; hence they decided to stay home.
sceneCN: 这里 hence 是「因此」（第 1 个义项）；句意：路上结了冰，因此他们决定待在家里。

senses.title: For this reason
senses.definition: as a result of what has just been said
senses.definitionCN: 由于刚才所说的事
senses.example: The roads were icy; hence they decided to stay home.
senses.exampleCN: 路上结了冰，因此他们决定待在家里。
senses.why: This is the common logical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是常见的因果义项。

senses.title: From this time
senses.definition: from this time onward
senses.definitionCN: 从此时起往后
senses.example: The custom began and has continued for years hence.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗开始了，并在此后多年延续。
senses.why: The old sense points forward in time.
senses.whyCN: 这一古老义项指向未来的时间。

intro.en: Hence began as a word meaning from here.
intro.cn: hence 最初表示「从这里」。

items.en: Hionan meant from this place.
items.cn: hionan 意为从这个地方。

items.en: Henness meant from here.
items.cn: henness 意为从这里。

items.en: The word moved from place to cause.
items.cn: 这个词从地点转向原因。

items.en: Hence came to mean for this reason.
items.cn: hence 逐渐表示因此。

items.en: Hence also kept the sense of time ahead.
items.cn: hence 也保留了未来时间的含义。

note.en: Hence is compared with look-alike words and with other linking words.
note.cn: 把 hence 与形近词以及其他连接词作比较。

entries.definition: from that place
entries.definitionCN: 从那里

entries.definition: from what place
entries.definitionCN: 从何处

entries.definition: because, or from a past time
entries.definitionCN: 因为；自从

entries.definition: for that reason
entries.definitionCN: 因此

entries.definition: in this way or for this reason
entries.definitionCN: 如此；因此

entries.definition: as a result
entries.definitionCN: 结果

normalIntro.en: Hence points to the result, and in older use to the time ahead.
normalIntro.cn: hence 指向结果，在较古的用法里也指向今后的时间。

normal.en: The roads were icy; hence they decided to stay home.
normal.cn: 路上结了冰，因此他们决定待在家里。

normal.en: He was late, hence the cold dinner.
normal.cn: 他回来晚了，因此饭菜都凉了。

normal.en: The town lies by the river, hence its name.
normal.cn: 这座镇子坐落在河畔，因此得名。

normal.en: Years hence, the story may still be told.
normal.cn: 多年以后，这个故事也许还会被讲起。

normal.en: The plan failed, hence the long meeting.
normal.cn: 计划失败了，因此开了这么长的会。

abstract.en: Hence is a small bridge from a cause to its shadow.
abstract.cn: hence 是从原因通向其影子的一座小桥。

abstract.en: What is done here echoes hence in another life.
abstract.cn: 在此处做下的事，会在另一种生活里回响。

abstract.en: Every hence hides a so that someone forgot.
abstract.cn: 每一个「因此」背后，都藏着一句被忘掉的「所以」。

examples.en: The roads were icy; hence they decided to stay home.
examples.cn: 路上结了冰，因此他们决定待在家里。

examples.en: He was late, hence the cold dinner.
examples.cn: 他回来晚了，因此饭菜都凉了。

examples.en: The town lies by the river, hence its name.
examples.cn: 这座镇子坐落在河畔，因此得名。

dict_mnemonic.text: hence 是「因此」，也可表示「从此」；hence the name 是因此得名，years hence 是若干年以后，and hence 也是因此在书面语中的说法。

root: 来自古英语 hionan（从这里），中古英语写作 henness；由空间上的「从这里」引申为逻辑上的「由这一点」，于是表示因此，也保留了时间上「此后」的旧义。

sensesIntro.en: Hence means for this reason, or from this time onward.
sensesIntro.cn: hence 表示因此，或从此时起往后。

core.en: A line drawn from a cause to its result.
core.cn: 从原因拉向结果的一条线。

branches.en: The roads were icy; hence they decided to stay home.
branches.cn: 路上结了冰，因此他们决定待在家里。

branches.en: Years hence, the story may still be told.
branches.cn: 多年以后，这个故事也许还会被讲起。

branches.en: From this point to that point, in logic or in time.
branches.cn: 从这一点到那一点，无论在逻辑还是时间上。

branches.en: He was late, hence the cold dinner.
branches.cn: 他回来晚了，因此饭菜都凉了。

branches.en: The plan failed, hence the long meeting.
branches.cn: 计划失败了，因此开了这么长的会。

intro.en: Hence is a fixed adverb, but it appears in a few set phrases.
intro.cn: hence 是固定副词，但出现在一些固定短语中。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，来自古英语。

items.example: Henceforth the rules will be strict.
items.exampleCN: 从今以后规则会很严格。

items.meaning: that is why it is called so
items.example: It is white, hence the name Snow Hill.
items.exampleCN: 它是白色的，因此得名雪山。

items.meaning: that is why it was late
items.example: The bridge was closed, hence the delay.
The soil is rich, and hence the crops grow well.
items.exampleCN: 土壤肥沃，因此庄稼长得好。

items.example: Years hence, the town may be a city.
items.exampleCN: 多年以后，这镇子也许会变成城市。

items.example: The road is steep, hence why we walked.
items.exampleCN: 路很陡，这就是我们步行的原因。

definition_en: an animal that feeds chiefly on plants, including grasses, leaves, fruits, seeds and sometimes algae
core_image: 一头牛低头啃食草甸，嘴角挂着草屑，身后的草地被啃出一道道弧线
scene: 这里指「食草动物」。 The deer is a browser herbivore that strips leaves from shrubs rather than grazing the open meadow.
sceneCN: 这里 herbivore 指「植食动物」（第 1 个义项：以植物为主要食物）；这种鹿是啃食灌木枝叶的植食动物，而不是在开阔草地上放牧。图中可辨识物件：牛、草甸、灌木枝叶、被啃出的弧线。

pos.zh: 食草动物；植食动物（可数，复数 herbivores）

collocations.zh: 放牧型植食动物；吃草类
啃食型植食动物；吃枝叶类
专性植食动物；必须吃植物才能存活
植食诱导防御；植物因被啃食而产生的化学防御

senses.title: An animal that eats plants
senses.titleCN: 植食动物：以植物为主要食物
senses.definition: an animal whose diet consists mainly of plant material such as grass, leaves, fruit or seeds
senses.definitionCN: 指以草、叶、果实或种子等植物材料为主要食物的动物
senses.example: The savanna supports herds of large herbivores during the wet season.
senses.exampleCN: 雨季时，稀树草原养活了成群的巨型植食动物。
senses.why: The word names a dietary class by its food source, so the definition is about what enters the mouth, not about teeth or hooves.
senses.whyCN: 这个词按食物来源命名食性类别，定义关注的是吃进嘴里的东西，而不是牙齿或蹄子。

senses.title: Grazers and browsers
senses.titleCN: 放牧型与啃食型：两种取食方式
senses.definition: a herbivore classified by feeding style, either cropping grass low to the ground or stripping leaves and twigs from shrubs and trees
senses.definitionCN: 指按取食方式分类的植食动物：或贴地啃食草类，或摘取灌木与树木的枝叶
senses.example: Grazing herbivores keep the grassland short, while browsing herbivores reach into the canopy.
senses.exampleCN: 放牧型植食动物把草地压短，啃食型则伸进树冠取食。
senses.why: Ecology splits the class by height of feeding, because grass and browse regrow differently under the same animal pressure.
senses.whyCN: 生态学按取食高度细分这一类，因为草与枝叶在同样取食压力下再生方式不同。

senses.title: Gut and fermentation
senses.titleCN: 消化道与发酵：靠微生物分解纤维素
senses.definition: a herbivore defined by its digestive arrangement, such as a rumen or a hindgut, where microbes break down cellulose
senses.definitionCN: 指按消化结构界定的植食动物，如具有瘤胃或后肠，由微生物分解纤维素
senses.example: As a ruminant herbivore, the cow relies on rumen microbes to digest grass.
senses.exampleCN: 作为反刍型植食动物，牛依靠瘤胃微生物消化草料。
senses.why: Plants are tough, so herbivores are defined as much by the microbial partnership in their gut as by their food.
senses.whyCN: 植物很坚韧，因此植食动物既由食物界定，也同样由肠道中的微生物伙伴界定。

senses.title: Obligate versus facultative
senses.titleCN: 专性与兼性：能否靠植物独活
senses.definition: a herbivore that must eat plants to survive, as opposed to one that eats plants only when other food is scarce
senses.definitionCN: 指必须吃植物才能存活的植食动物，与仅在其他食物稀缺时才吃植物的兼性者相对
senses.example: The koala is an obligate herbivore restricted to a few eucalypt species.
senses.exampleCN: 考拉是专性植食动物，只吃少数几种桉树。
senses.why: The distinction separates a fixed diet from an opportunistic one, which matters when habitats change.
senses.whyCN: 这一区分把固定食性与机会性食性分开，在生境变化时尤为重要。

senses.title: Herbivore as ecosystem engineer
senses.titleCN: 生态系统工程师：植食动物塑造植被
senses.definition: a herbivore whose feeding and trampling reshape plant communities and therefore the habitats of other species
senses.definitionCN: 指其取食与踩踏重塑植物群落、进而改变其他物种生境的植食动物
senses.example: The elephant is a herbivore that engineers the savanna by pushing over trees.
senses.exampleCN: 大象是一种植食动物，它推倒树木，从而改造稀树草原。
senses.why: The label stops describing a diet and starts describing a force: what the animal eats determines what everyone else can eat.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签不再只描述食性，而开始描述一种力量：它吃什么决定了别人能吃什么。

senses.title: Plant defence against herbivores
senses.titleCN: 植物的防御：针对植食动物的化学与物理屏障
senses.definition: the role of a herbivore as the pressure that selects for thorns, toxins and tough tissues in plants
senses.definitionCN: 指植食动物作为选择压力，促使植物演化出刺、毒素与坚韧组织的角色
senses.example: Thorns and bitter alkaloids are defences aimed at herbivores.
senses.exampleCN: 刺与苦味生物碱是针对植食动物的防御。
senses.why: The word appears on the attacking side of a coevolutionary arms race, which is why plant defences are named after it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出现在共同演化军备竞赛的进攻一方，因此植物的防御以它为名。

senses.title: Marine herbivores
senses.titleCN: 海洋植食者：海草与藻类的取食者
senses.definition: an aquatic animal that feeds on seagrass, algae or other marine plants
senses.definitionCN: 指以海草、藻类或其他海洋植物为食的水生动物
senses.example: Sea turtles and some reef fish are marine herbivores that keep algae short.
senses.exampleCN: 海龟与部分礁鱼是海洋植食者，它们把藻类压短。
senses.why: The class crosses the shoreline: wherever there is plant tissue, there is a herbivore adapted to eat it.
senses.whyCN: 这一类跨越海岸线：凡有植物组织的地方，就有适应取食它的植食动物。

senses.title: Herbivore in casual speech
senses.titleCN: 口语用法：素食者或食性比喻
senses.definition: an informal or humorous use for a person who eats a plant-based diet, or for a mild, non-aggressive party
senses.definitionCN: 口语或戏谑用法，指以植物性饮食为主的人，或指温和不具攻击性的一方
senses.example: He calls himself a herbivore, though he still eats eggs.
senses.exampleCN: 他自称植食者，不过仍然吃蛋。
senses.why: The zoological word has drifted into diet talk, where it is friendlier and less doctrinal than vegetarian.
senses.whyCN: 这个动物学词汇漂移到饮食话题，在那里比「素食者」这一说法更轻松、更少教条色彩。

intro.en: Herbivore is a modern scientific compound from Latin herba 'grass, herb' and vorare 'to devour', literally 'plant devourer'.
intro.cn: herbivore 是近代科学复合词，由拉丁语 herba「草、草本」与 vorare「吞食」构成，字面即「吞食植物者」。

items.en: Herba meant grass, green plants or an herb, and it also underlies herb, herbage and herbaceous in English.
items.cn: herba 指草、绿色植物或香草，也是英语 herb、herbage、herbaceous 的来源。

items.en: Vorare meant to devour or swallow whole. It is the second half of carnivore, omnivore, insectivore and voracious.
items.cn: vorare 意为吞食、整口吞下，它是 carnivore、omnivore、insectivore 与 voracious 的后半部分。

items.en: The compound was formed in modern scientific Latin, and French zoologist Georges Cuvier is usually credited with popularising the dietary classification in the early nineteenth century. The exact coining is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个复合词在近代科学拉丁语中形成；一般认为法国动物学家居维叶在 19 世纪早期推广了这套食性分类，但确切的造词者存疑。

items.en: Zoology standardised the triad herbivore, carnivore and omnivore, turning a descriptive compound into a classification system.
items.cn: 动物学把 herbivore、carnivore、omnivore 确立为三分法，把一个描述性复合词变成分类体系。

items.en: The pattern later produced insectivore, frugivore, folivore and nectarivore, each naming a specific plant or animal food.
items.cn: 这一模式后来派生出 insectivore、frugivore、folivore、nectarivore，各自命名特定的植物或动物食物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vore ending and must be told apart by the first element; the near-meaning group separates diet class from feeding style.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -vore 结尾，须靠前半部分区分；近义组区分食性类别与取食方式。

entries.definition: An animal that eats mainly animal flesh. The first element is Latin caro 'flesh', so the two words differ at the stem, not the ending.
entries.definitionCN: 指以动物肉为主食的动物。前半是拉丁语 caro「肉」，因此两词区别在词干而非词尾。

entries.definition: An animal that eats both plant and animal food. The first element omni- 'all' marks the broader diet.
entries.definitionCN: 指既吃植物也吃动物的动物。前半 omni-「全部」标出更宽的食性。

entries.definition: The adjective form meaning plant-eating. Herbivore is the noun for the animal, so the two cannot swap places.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式，意为植食的。herbivore 是动物的名词，两者不能互换位置。

entries.definition: A herbivore that crops grass and low vegetation. It is a subset of herbivore, defined by feeding height rather than diet alone.
entries.definitionCN: 指啃食草类与低矮植被的植食动物。它是植食动物的子集，按取食高度而非仅按食性界定。

entries.definition: A herbivore that strips leaves and twigs from shrubs and trees. Do not confuse it with the web browser.
entries.definitionCN: 指摘食灌木与树木枝叶的植食动物。注意不要与网络浏览器混淆。

entries.definition: A herbivore specialising in leaves. It is narrower than herbivore, which also covers grass, fruit and seed eaters.
entries.definitionCN: 指专食树叶的植食动物，比 herbivore 更窄，后者还包括吃草、果实与种子者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: herba 'grass' + vorare 'devour': the plant devourer.
normal.cn: herba「草」+ vorare「吞食」：吞食植物者。

normal.en: Read -vore as 'eater' and the first half names the food: herbi-, carni-, omni-, insecti-.
normal.cn: 把 -vore 读作「吃……者」，前半部分就是食物：herbi-、carni-、omni-、insecti-。

normal.en: The family runs herb, herbaceous, herbage, herbicide, herbivorous and herbivory.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 herb、herbaceous、herbage、herbicide、herbivorous、herbivory。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: grazing herbivore, browsing herbivore, obligate herbivore, herbivore population.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：放牧型植食动物、啃食型植食动物、专性植食动物、植食动物种群。

normal.en: Cuvier is usually credited with the dietary triad in the early 1800s, though the coining is uncertain.
normal.cn: 一般认为居维叶在 1800 年代初提出这套食性三分法，但造词者存疑。

abstract.en: Picture a cow tearing grass with a sideways sweep of its head.
abstract.cn: 想象一头牛把头一甩，撕下一把草。

abstract.en: Picture a deer standing on hind legs to reach leaves above the browse line.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鹿立起后腿，够取啃食线以上的树叶。

abstract.en: Picture an elephant pushing a tree over so the whole herd can feed.
abstract.cn: 想象大象推倒一棵树，让整群都能取食。

examples.en: Large herbivores keep the savanna open by eating young trees.
examples.cn: 大型植食动物吃掉落树幼苗，使稀树草原保持开阔。

examples.en: The koala is an obligate herbivore with a narrow diet.
examples.cn: 考拉是食性很窄的专性植食动物。

examples.en: Plant toxins evolved as defences against herbivores.
examples.cn: 植物毒素是作为抵御植食动物的防御演化出来的。

dict_mnemonic.text: herb（草本）+ vore（吃……者）→ 吃草的东西 → herbivore 食草动物

root: 拉丁 herba「草、草本」+ vorare「吞食」→ 近代科学拉丁语 herbivorus／herbivore「吞食植物者」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the plain diet label and then add feeding height, gut design, obligation, ecosystem effects, plant defence, marine life and casual speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从最朴素的食性标签开始，再依次加入取食高度、消化道设计、专性程度、生态效应、植物防御、海洋生活与口语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cow sweeping grass into its mouth, leaving curved bite marks.
core.cn: 核心意象：牛把草扫进嘴里，留下弧形咬痕。

branches.en: DIET: the base sense names an animal by what it eats.
branches.cn: 食性：基本义按吃什么来命名动物。

branches.en: STYLE: grazer and browser split the class by feeding height.
branches.cn: 方式：放牧型与啃食型按取食高度细分这一类。

branches.en: PHYSIOLOGY AND NECESSITY: gut microbes and obligation decide whether plants can be the only food.
branches.cn: 生理与必要性：肠道微生物与专性程度决定植物能否成为唯一食物。

branches.en: FORCE: the herbivore shapes plant communities, and plants evolve defences against it.
branches.cn: 力量：植食动物塑造植物群落，植物则演化出针对它的防御。

branches.en: RANGE: the label crosses into the sea and into casual talk about diets.
branches.cn: 范围：这个标签跨入海洋，也跨入口语中的饮食话题。

intro.en: Herbivore is a two-part scientific compound, and the same -vore ending builds a whole family of diet words.
intro.cn: herbivore 是两部分构成的科学复合词，同一个 -vore 结尾还能造出一整族食性词汇。

latinIntro.en: Herba supplies the food, vorare supplies the eating, and the compound was fixed in modern scientific Latin before entering English.
latinIntro.cn: herba 提供食物，vorare 提供吃，这个复合词在近代科学拉丁语中定型后才进入英语。

items.exampleCN: 这片草甸养活着好几种植食动物。
植食性昆虫把叶子吃光了。

items.meaning: the act or process of plant eating
items.example: Herbivory removes a third of the leaf mass.
items.exampleCN: 植食带走了三分之一的叶量。

items.meaning: a plant used for food, medicine or flavour
items.meaningCN: 用于食物、药物或调味的植物
items.exampleCN: 园子里种着烹饪用的香草。

items.example: The border is planted with herbaceous perennials.
items.exampleCN: 花境里种的是草本多年生植物。

items.example: The field was cleared with herbicide.
items.exampleCN: 这块田用除草剂清除了杂草。
这只食肉动物黄昏时狩猎。

items.meaning: animal eating both plants and flesh
items.meaningCN: 既吃植物也吃肉的动物
items.example: The omnivore switches between berries and insects.
items.exampleCN: 这种杂食动物在浆果与昆虫之间切换。
这些毛虫是贪食的取食者。

definition_zh: 植食性的；以植物为食的
definition_en: describing an animal whose diet consists mainly of plants, or a structure adapted to eating plant material
core_image: 一排宽大的臼齿在咀嚼干草，齿面被磨成水平的磨盘
scene: 这里指「植食性的」。 The herbivorous dinosaurs had broad grinding teeth suited to ferns and cycads.
sceneCN: 这里 herbivorous 指「植食性的」（第 1 个义项：以植物为主要食物）；这些植食性恐龙有宽阔的研磨齿，适合吃蕨类与苏铁。图中可辨识物件：臼齿、干草、蕨叶、苏铁。

pos.zh: 植食性的；以植物为食的（比较级 more herbivorous，最高级 most herbivorous）

senses.title: Plant-eating by diet
senses.titleCN: 植食性：食谱以植物为主
senses.definition: describing an animal whose food is mainly plant material
senses.definitionCN: 描述以植物材料为主要食物的动物
senses.example: Most large mammals on the plain are herbivorous.
senses.exampleCN: 平原上的大型哺乳动物大多是植食性的。
senses.why: The adjective attaches the diet class to a particular animal, so it answers what kind of eater this species is.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把食性类别挂到具体动物上，用来回答这个物种属于哪类取食者。

senses.title: Teeth built for plants
senses.titleCN: 齿型适应：宽平的研磨面
senses.definition: describing dental or jaw anatomy adapted to grinding tough plant fibres rather than shearing flesh
senses.definitionCN: 描述适应研磨坚韧植物纤维而非切割肉类的牙齿或颌部结构
senses.example: The herbivorous jaw is deep and the molars are flat.
senses.exampleCN: 植食性的颌部厚实，臼齿扁平。
senses.why: Anatomy carries the diet: flat grinding surfaces are the physical signature of a plant eater.
senses.whyCN: 解剖结构携带着食性信息：平坦的研磨面就是植食者的物理签名。

senses.title: Gut adapted to fibre
senses.titleCN: 消化道适应：长肠与发酵腔
senses.definition: describing a digestive tract that is long or chambered enough for microbes to break down cellulose
senses.definitionCN: 描述足够长或具有发酵腔、可供微生物分解纤维素的消化道
senses.example: Herbivorous mammals have a caecum or rumen for fermentation.
senses.exampleCN: 植食性哺乳动物有盲肠或瘤胃用于发酵。
senses.why: Cellulose resists ordinary digestion, so the adjective also marks an animal that houses microbes.
senses.whyCN: 纤维素难以普通消化，因此这个形容词也标出体内养着微生物的动物。

senses.title: Herbivorous insects
senses.titleCN: 植食性昆虫：把植物当全部食物
senses.definition: describing insects that feed on leaves, sap, wood, seeds or nectar
senses.definitionCN: 描述取食叶片、汁液、木材、种子或花蜜的昆虫
senses.example: Herbivorous beetles account for much of the damage in the plantation.
senses.exampleCN: 植食性甲虫造成了种植园里的大部分损害。
senses.why: Most animal species are insects, and most of them are plant eaters, so this is the largest herbivorous group on land.
senses.whyCN: 动物物种以昆虫为主，而昆虫大多吃植物，因此这是陆地上最大的植食类群。

senses.title: Strictly herbivorous
senses.titleCN: 严格植食：完全不吃动物性食物
senses.definition: describing a diet with no animal material at all, as opposed to occasional omnivory
senses.definitionCN: 描述完全不含动物性食物的食性，与偶尔杂食相对
senses.example: The species is strictly herbivorous and will not take carrion.
senses.exampleCN: 该物种严格植食，不会取食腐肉。
senses.why: The adverb matters because many herbivores occasionally eat insects, which blurs the boundary with omnivory.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词很重要，因为许多植食动物偶尔吃昆虫，从而模糊了与杂食的边界。

senses.title: Herbivorous dinosaurs
senses.titleCN: 植食恐龙：古生物中的取食类群
senses.definition: describing extinct reptiles identified as plant eaters from teeth, gut contents or coprolites
senses.definitionCN: 描述依据牙齿、胃内容物或粪化石判定为植食的已灭绝爬行动物
senses.example: Herbivorous dinosaurs ranged from low browsers to high-reaching sauropods.
senses.exampleCN: 植食恐龙从低处啃食者一直分布到高处的蜥脚类。
senses.why: Palaeontology uses the adjective for fossil taxa whose diet must be inferred rather than observed.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学把这个形容词用于食性只能推断、无法直接观察的化石类群。

senses.title: Marine plant eaters
senses.titleCN: 海洋植食：吃海草与藻类
senses.definition: describing aquatic animals that graze seagrass, macroalgae or epilithic algae
senses.definitionCN: 描述啃食海草、大型藻类或附着藻类的水生动物
senses.example: Herbivorous fish keep the reef free of smothering algae.
senses.exampleCN: 植食性鱼类让礁体免于被藻类覆盖。
senses.why: Reef health depends on these grazers, so the adjective becomes a management label.
senses.whyCN: 礁体健康依赖这些啃食者，因此这个形容词也成了管理标签。

senses.title: Figurative and dietary use
senses.titleCN: 比喻与饮食用法：温和或素食
senses.definition: used informally of a person's plant-based diet, or humorously of a mild, non-aggressive temperament
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指个人的植物性饮食，或戏谑地指温和、不具攻击性的性情
senses.example: He describes himself as herbivorous but still eats fish.
senses.exampleCN: 他自称植食，不过仍吃鱼。
senses.why: The adjective softens a dietary choice into a temperament metaphor, which is why it appears in casual writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把饮食选择软化成一种性情比喻，因此常见于随笔。

intro.en: Herbivorous is the Latin adjective herbivorus, built from herba 'grass' and vorare 'devour', and it predates the English noun herbivore.
intro.cn: herbivorous 是拉丁形容词 herbivorus，由 herba「草」与 vorare「吞食」构成，其出现早于英语名词 herbivore。

items.en: Herba covered grass and green plants generally, not only culinary herbs.
items.cn: herba 泛指草与绿色植物，不只是烹饪用的香草。

items.en: Vorare meant to swallow or devour, and the adjective -vorus 'eating' was used in compounds such as carnivorus.
items.cn: vorare 意为吞咽、吞食，形容词成分 -vorus「吃……的」用于 carnivorus 这类复合词。

items.en: Herbivorus belongs to modern scientific Latin, where diet adjectives were formed freely from Latin roots. Its exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: herbivorus 属近代科学拉丁语，这类食性形容词可由拉丁词根自由构成；确切首用存疑。

items.en: English adopted herbivorous in the nineteenth century alongside the noun. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在 19 世纪与名词同时期采用 herbivorous；确切首见书证存疑。

items.en: The same pattern produced carnivorous, omnivorous, insectivorous and frugivorous, so the ending -ivorous became a productive classifier.
items.cn: 同一模式造出 carnivorous、omnivorous、insectivorous、frugivorous，词尾 -ivorous 因而成为能产的分类成分。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vorous ending; the near-meaning group separates plant eating from related but narrower labels.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -vorous 结尾；近义组把植食与更窄的相关标签区分开。

entries.definition: The animal itself. It cannot modify another noun, so a plant-eating dinosaur is a herbivorous dinosaur, not a herbivore dinosaur.
entries.definitionCN: 指动物本身。它不能修饰其他名词，因此应说 herbivorous dinosaur，而不是 herbivore dinosaur。

entries.definition: Describes a flesh diet. The stem caro- 'flesh' is the only difference, and the two adjectives mark opposite diets.
entries.definitionCN: 描述食肉。词干 caro-「肉」是唯一差别，两个形容词标示相反的食性。

entries.definition: Describes a mixed diet of plants and animals. The stem omni- 'all' widens the diet beyond herbivorous.
entries.definitionCN: 描述植物与动物混合的食性。词干 omni-「全部」把食性拓宽到植食之外。

entries.definition: Describes a diet of leaves specifically. It is narrower than herbivorous, which also covers grass, fruit and seeds.
entries.definitionCN: 描述专食树叶的食性。它比 herbivorous 更窄，后者还包括草、果实与种子。

entries.definition: Describes a diet of grasses and cereals. It is a rare technical term, narrower than herbivorous.
entries.definitionCN: 描述以禾草与谷物为食。它是罕见的技术词，比 herbivorous 更窄。

entries.definition: A transparent compound meaning the same as herbivorous but without the scientific register.
entries.definitionCN: 透明的复合词，含义与 herbivorous 相同，但不带科学语域。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实后缀、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: herba 'grass' + -vorous 'eating': eating grass and plants.
normal.cn: herba「草」+ -vorous「吃……的」：吃草与植物。

normal.en: Swap the stem to change the diet: herbi-, carni-, omni-, insecti-, frugi-.
normal.cn: 换词干就换食性：herbi-、carni-、omni-、insecti-、frugi-。

normal.en: Typical phrases: herbivorous animal, herbivorous dinosaur, herbivorous insect, strictly herbivorous.
normal.cn: 典型搭配：植食动物、植食性恐龙、植食性昆虫、严格植食。

normal.en: Flat molars and a fermentation chamber are the anatomical tells of this adjective.
normal.cn: 扁平臼齿与发酵腔是这个形容词的解剖学线索。

normal.en: The noun is herbivore and the process is herbivory; keep the three forms apart.
normal.cn: 名词是 herbivore，过程是 herbivory；三种形式要分清。

abstract.en: Picture molars grinding dry grass into a flat paste.
abstract.cn: 想象臼齿把干草磨成扁平的糊。

abstract.en: Picture a caterpillar stripping a leaf down to its veins.
abstract.cn: 想象毛虫把一片叶子啃到只剩叶脉。

abstract.en: Picture a fish scraping algae off coral so the coral can still see light.
abstract.cn: 想象一条鱼把藻类从珊瑚上刮掉，让珊瑚仍能见到光。

examples.en: The fossil's flat molars mark it as herbivorous.
examples.cn: 这块化石的扁平臼齿表明它是植食性的。

examples.en: Herbivorous insects remove a large share of the canopy each summer.
examples.cn: 每年夏天，植食性昆虫带走大量树冠叶片。

examples.en: The lake's herbivorous fish keep the water clear of algae.
examples.cn: 湖中的植食性鱼类让水体免于藻类覆盖。

dict_mnemonic.text: herbivore（食草动物）+ ous（……的）→ 食草的 → herbivorous 植食性的

root: 拉丁 herba「草」+ vorare「吞食」→ 科学拉丁语 herbivorus「吃植物的」→ 英语 herbivorous。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one adjective to diet, teeth, gut, insects, strictness, fossils, reefs and casual talk.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个形容词用于食性、牙齿、消化道、昆虫、严格程度、化石、礁体与口语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: flat molars grinding dry grass into paste.
core.cn: 核心意象：扁平臼齿把干草磨成糊。

branches.en: DIET: the base sense says the food is plant material.
branches.cn: 食性：基本义说食物是植物材料。

branches.en: ANATOMY: teeth and gut carry the diet in bone and tissue.
branches.cn: 解剖：牙齿与消化道把食性写进骨骼与组织。

branches.en: SCOPE: insects dominate the class, and strictness separates it from omnivory.
branches.cn: 范围：昆虫在这一类中占主导，严格程度则把它与杂食分开。

branches.en: APPLIED FIELDS: palaeontology infers it from fossils, reef management relies on it.
branches.cn: 应用领域：古生物学从化石推断它，礁体管理依赖它。

branches.en: DRIFT: the adjective becomes a gentle metaphor for diet and temperament.
branches.cn: 漂移：这个形容词成为饮食与性情的温和比喻。

intro.en: Herbivorous is a Latin adjective whose ending -vorous is a productive classifier in zoology.
intro.cn: herbivorous 是拉丁形容词，其结尾 -vorous 在动物学中是能产的分类成分。

latinIntro.en: Herba is the plant, vorare the eating, and -vorus the adjectival form of the eating verb.
latinIntro.cn: herba 是植物，vorare 是吃，-vorus 是吃的动词的形容词形式。

items.example: Each herbivore has its preferred grass.
items.exampleCN: 每种植食动物都有偏好的草。
植食程度随叶片硬度变化。

items.example: Omnivorous birds take grain and grubs.
items.exampleCN: 杂食鸟类既吃谷物也吃幼虫。

items.meaning: a plant valued for food or medicine
items.meaningCN: 用于食物或药物的植物
items.example: The herb grows in damp shade.
items.exampleCN: 这种草本长在潮湿的荫处。

core_image: 一大群动物挤在一起，朝着同一个方向移动
scene: 一群牛在河边吃草。A herd of cattle grazed by the river.
sceneCN: 这里 herd 是「畜群」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一群牛在河边吃草。

senses.title: Group of animals
senses.definition: a large group of animals that feed or move together
senses.definitionCN: 一起觅食或移动的一大群动物
senses.example: A herd of cattle grazed by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 一群牛在河边吃草。
senses.why: This is the basic animal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的动物义项。

senses.title: Crowd
senses.definition: a large crowd of people, often acting together
senses.definitionCN: 常一起行动的一大群人
senses.example: A herd of fans pushed toward the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 一大群粉丝朝大门涌去。
senses.why: People moving like animals take the same word.
senses.whyCN: 像动物一样移动的人群也借用这个词。

senses.title: Drive animals
senses.definition: to make animals or people move together in one direction
senses.definitionCN: 使动物或人朝同一方向移动
senses.example: The farmer herded the sheep into the pen.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫把羊赶进围栏。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb of driving.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示驱赶的动词。

items.cn: 该词根指一群动物。

items.cn: heord 意为畜群。

items.en: Herd also named a crowd of people.
items.cn: herd 也指人群。

items.cn: herd 成为驱赶动物的动词。

entries.definitionCN: 兽群

normalIntro.cn: herd 是许多动物如同一体地移动，动词则是牧人做的事。
