definition_zh: 牧人；畜群看管者；牧场雇工；宗教比喻中的牧养者
definition_en: a person who watches over and drives a herd of animals, either for a family or for an employer
core_image: 一个裹着旧毯子的人坐在羊栏边的石头上，手里的牧杖横在膝上，眼睛跟着每一只走动的羊。
scene: 夜里风大，羊栏边的石头上坐着一个人，牧杖横放膝头，眼睛跟着每一只羊。An old herdsman watched the flock while the others slept.
sceneCN: 这里 herdsman 指「看管并驱赶畜群的牧人」（第 1 个义项：以照看一群牲畜为职责的人）；句意为一位老牧人在其他人睡着时看守羊群。可辨识物件：羊栏、石头、牧杖、旧毯子、羊群。

pos.zh: 牧人；畜群看管者；（比喻）牧养者

derivatives.zh: 古英语 heord（畜群）→ 由「一群牲畜」转为「把牲畜聚成一群」
herd + -er（施事后缀）→ 牧人，语义偏重日常照看者
herdsman 的 man 换为 woman → 女牧人，语义仅改性别
herdsman + -ship（技艺或身份后缀）→ 牧放的本领与职责，语义由人转为能力
herd + -ing（动作名词后缀）→ 放牧这项劳动，语义由人转为活动

senses.title: A person who watches a herd
senses.definition: a person whose job is to keep a group of animals together and safe while they feed
senses.definitionCN: 职责是在牲畜吃草时把它们聚在一起并保其安全的人
senses.example: An old herdsman watched the flock while the others slept.
senses.exampleCN: 一位老牧人在其他人睡着时看守羊群。
senses.why: herd plus man simply names the person attached to the herd, so the basic sense is the keeper himself.
senses.whyCN: herd 加 man 直接指与畜群相连的人，因此最基本的义项就是看管者本人。

senses.title: Hired labour on a ranch
senses.definition: a paid worker who tends stock on land owned by someone else
senses.definitionCN: 在他人所有的土地上照看牲畜、领取报酬的工人
senses.example: The ranch hired two herdsmen for the lambing season.
senses.exampleCN: 牧场在产羔季雇了两名牧工。
senses.why: once herding became wage work, the title split off from the owner and named the employee.
senses.whyCN: 一旦放牧变成雇佣劳动，这个称呼就与所有者分开，用来指受雇者。

senses.title: A keeper of one kind of animal
senses.definition: a specialist who tends a single species, such as cattle, goats or camels
senses.definitionCN: 只照看一种牲畜的专门人员，如牛、山羊或骆驼
senses.example: The cattle herdsman knew which cow would calve first.
senses.exampleCN: 牛倌知道哪头母牛会先产犊。
senses.why: where a village keeps several species, the work divides, and the title takes the animal's name in front.
senses.whyCN: 当村庄饲养数种牲畜时，工作会分门，称呼就在前面加上牲畜之名。

senses.title: Owner or manager of stock
senses.titleCN: 牲畜的所有者或管理者
senses.definition: in older usage, the person who owns or directs the herd rather than only tending it
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，指拥有或支配畜群的人，而不只是照看者
senses.example: The herdsman whose brand marked the cattle also decided where they grazed.
senses.exampleCN: 给牛打上烙印的畜主也决定它们去哪里吃草。
senses.why: before specialised labour, the keeper and the owner were often the same man, and the word covered both.
senses.whyCN: 在分工之前，看管者与所有者常是同一个人，这个词因而兼指两者。

senses.title: A religious figure who tends souls
senses.definition: a minister pictured as a shepherd guiding and protecting a congregation
senses.definitionCN: 被比作牧羊人、引导并保护会众的宗教人员
senses.example: The sermon called every pastor a herdsman of people, not of sheep.
senses.exampleCN: 布道把每位牧师称为人的牧人，而不是羊的牧人。
senses.why: the Bible uses shepherd imagery for leaders, and English sermons carried that imagery into herdsman language.
senses.whyCN: 《圣经》用牧羊人的形象指领导者，英语布道把这一形象带进了 herdsman 的说法。

senses.title: An archetype in myth and literature
senses.titleCN: 神话与文学中的牧人原型
senses.definition: the stock figure of the lonely keeper, often a guide, a singer or a witness in stories
senses.definitionCN: 故事中孤独看管者的定型形象，常充当引路人、歌者或见证者
senses.example: In the legend the herdsman is the only one who sees the stranger arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 传说中，牧人是唯一看见陌生人到来的人。
senses.why: a keeper who sits through the night sees what sleeping villages miss, so stories place him at the edge of events.
senses.whyCN: 守夜的人看见睡着的村庄看不见的事，因此故事把他放在事件的边缘。

senses.title: One who guides a crowd
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：带领并照看一群人的人
senses.definition: a leader described as keeping a group together and moving it safely, with a hint of care
senses.definitionCN: 被描述为把一群人聚住并安全带走的人，含照料意味
senses.example: The strike leader acted as a herdsman for two hundred frightened workers.
senses.exampleCN: 罢工领袖像牧人一样带着两百名惊恐的工人。
senses.why: guiding people and guiding animals share the same gestures, so the farm title transfers with its protective tone.
senses.whyCN: 带人和带牲畜的手势相同，因此这个农场称呼连同其保护口吻一起转移过来。

senses.title: Any keeper of a dependent group
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何照料并引导一群对象的人
senses.definition: anyone responsible for keeping a dependent collection together, whether animals, people or data
senses.definitionCN: 负责把一群依赖性的对象聚住并照看的任何人，无论对象是牲畜、人还是数据
senses.example: The archive's herdsman kept ten thousand files from drifting apart.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆的看管人让一万份文件不致散失。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the role: something scattered needs one person who holds it together.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留角色本身：散开的东西需要一个把它们聚住的人。

intro.en: Herdsman is an English compound of herd and man, with a genitive -s between them. Both parts are Old English and Germanic; no Latin element is involved.
intro.cn: herdsman 是 herd 与 man 的英语复合词，中间有属格 -s。两部分都属古英语与日耳曼语，不含拉丁成分。

items.en: Heord 'group of animals' is the first element; its Germanic shape is reconstructed, and the exact wider Indo-European link is disputed.
items.cn: heord「一群牲畜」是第一部分；其日耳曼语形式属重构，更广的印欧联系有争议。

items.en: Man meant 'human being, person' and still did when the compound formed; the modern restriction to an adult male came later.
items.cn: man 意为「人、人类」，复合词形成时仍是此义；后来才收窄为成年男性。

items.en: The -s is the old genitive ending, so herdsman originally meant 'the herd's man', the man belonging to the herd.
items.cn: 这个 -s 是古属格词尾，因此 herdsman 原意是「畜群的人」，即属于这群牲畜的人。

items.en: Middle English herdesman kept the compound for a professional keeper, alongside the shorter herd and herder.
items.cn: 中古英语 herdesman 保留了这个复合词，指职业看管者，同时还有更短的 herd 与 herder。

items.en: From the sixteenth century English sermons applied shepherd and herdsman imagery to clergy, adding the figurative sense.
items.cn: 从 16 世纪起，英语布道把牧羊人与牧人的形象用于神职人员，增添了比喻义。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the precise first written appearance of the compound is not fixed, and the pre-Germanic origin of heord remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个复合词确切的首次书面出现并无定说，heord 在日耳曼语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds titles from the same herding stock that differ only in formality or gender; group two holds words for people who look after animals or people.
note.cn: 第一组是同出放牧词源、只在正式程度或性别上不同的称呼；第二组是照看动物或照看人的邻近词。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a keeper of animals, formed with -er; herdsman is the older, more formal title.
entries.definitionCN: 指牲畜看管者的日常词，由 -er 构成；herdsman 是更古老、更正式的称呼。

entries.definition: The animals themselves, or the verb for driving them; it never names the keeper.
entries.definitionCN: 指牲畜本身，或指驱赶它们的动词，从不指看管者。

entries.definition: The same job with woman in place of man; the plural is herdswomen.
entries.definitionCN: 同一职业，把 man 换成 woman；复数为 herdswomen。

entries.definition: From sheep plus hierde 'herder', so it is a compound of a different animal and an older agent noun, not a variant of herdsman.
entries.definitionCN: 由 sheep 加 hierde「牧人」构成，是另一种牲畜与更古老施事名词的复合，并非 herdsman 的变体。

entries.definition: A rider who works cattle on open range; the word stresses horses and driving rather than daily watching.
entries.definitionCN: 在开阔牧场上骑马管牛的人；这个词强调马与驱赶，而非日常看管。

entries.definition: A farm worker who handles livestock; it is an agricultural job title rather than a cultural one.
entries.definitionCN: 料理牲畜的农场工人；它是农业职称，而非文化称呼。

entries.definition: A minister; its literal shepherd sense is historical, while herdsman keeps the animal sense alive.
entries.definitionCN: 牧师；其字面的牧人义已属历史，而 herdsman 仍保留牲畜义。

entries.definition: The owner or manager of a ranch; herdsman names the person who does the daily watching.
entries.definitionCN: 牧场所有者或经营者；herdsman 指做日常看管的人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real genitive compound, real relatives and real occupational phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的属格复合、真实同族词与真实职业搭配。

normal.en: herd + genitive -s + man: literally 'the herd's man'.
normal.cn: herd + 属格 -s + man：字面就是「畜群的人」。

normal.en: The family runs herd, herder, herding, herdsman, herdswoman, herdsmanship.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 herd、herder、herding、herdsman、herdswoman、herdsmanship。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the job: a cattle herdsman, a nomadic herdsman, the herdsman's staff.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这一职业：牛倌、游牧牧人、牧人的杖。

normal.en: Shepherd is a parallel compound, sheep plus the older agent noun hierde.
normal.cn: shepherd 是平行复合词，由 sheep 加更古老的施事名词 hierde 构成。

normal.en: The irregular plural herdsmen keeps the old genitive sound.
normal.cn: 不规则复数 herdsmen 保留了古属格的读音。

abstract.en: Picture one man awake at night so that a hundred animals can sleep standing up.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人夜里不睡，好让一百头牲畜能站着睡。

abstract.en: Picture a staff laid across a lap, doubling as a seat and a counting tool.
abstract.cn: 想象一根杖横在膝上，既是坐处也是数数的工具。

abstract.en: Picture a leader who walks behind the crowd so that no one is left at the edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一位带头人走在人群后面，好让边上没人被落下。

examples.en: The herdsman could name every animal in the flock by its markings.
examples.cn: 牧人能凭毛色花纹叫出羊群里每一只的名字。

examples.en: Wages for a herdsman are low, but the work comes with milk and wool.
examples.cn: 牧人的工资不高，但这活附带奶和羊毛。

examples.en: Novels often give the herdsman a song and no other possession.
examples.cn: 小说常给牧人一首歌，别的财产一概不给。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「herds（畜群）+ man（人）」——属于畜群的那个人 → 牧人、看管者

root: 古英语 heord「一群牲畜」+ 属格 -s + man「人」，字面为「畜群的人」；两部分皆属日耳曼语系，无拉丁成分。英语 herdsman。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one role: a person attached to a herd. The role is then read as a hired worker, a species specialist, an owner, a pastor, a mythic figure, a guide of people and finally any keeper of a dependent group.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个角色展开：一个属于畜群的人。这个角色再依次被读作雇工、单一畜种的专人、畜主、牧养者、神话人物、人群的引导者，最后读作任何依赖群体的看管者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person awake at the edge of a sleeping flock.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人醒着，守在一群睡着的牲畜旁边。

branches.en: KEEPER AND OWNER: the same title covers the man who watches and the man whose brand the animals carry.
branches.cn: 看管者与所有者：同一个称呼既指看羊的人，也指牲畜身上打着他烙印的人。

branches.en: DIVIDED LABOUR: hired hands and single-species specialists appear once herds grow beyond one family.
branches.cn: 分工：当畜群超过一户人家能管的规模，雇工与单一畜种的专人就出现了。

branches.en: SOULS AND STORIES: the night watcher becomes a pastor in sermons and a witness in legends.
branches.cn: 灵魂与故事：守夜人在布道里成了牧养者，在传说里成了见证者。

branches.en: GUIDE OF PEOPLE: the protective gestures of herding transfer to a leader of a crowd.
branches.cn: 人的引导者：放牧中保护性的手势转移到带领人群的人身上。

branches.en: ANY DEPENDENT GROUP: keep only the role, and files or data can need a keeper too.
branches.cn: 任何依赖群体：只保留角色，文件或数据也可以需要一个看管者。

intro.en: Herdsman is a two-part English compound with an old genitive ending; no Latin prefix or root takes part.
intro.cn: herdsman 是由两部分构成的英语复合词，中间带古属格词尾，不含拉丁前缀或词根。

latinIntro.en: This line has no Latin relative, so the Latin list is left empty; the parts are Old English and Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这一词线没有拉丁同族词，因此拉丁列表留空；各成分属古英语与日耳曼语。

items.example: The first element names the animals.
The older agent noun also survives inside shepherd.
items.exampleCN: 更古老的施事名词也残留在 shepherd 里。

items.example: The second element names the person, not the sex.
items.exampleCN: 第二部分指人，而不是指性别。

items.example: The ending makes herdsman literally 'the herd's man'.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾使 herdsman 字面成为「畜群的人」。

items.meaning: a group of animals; to drive them
items.example: The herd moved down the valley.

items.meaning: the skill and duty of tending stock
items.example: Herdsmanship was judged by the winter survival rate.
items.exampleCN: 放牧本领以越冬存活率来评判。

items.example: The herdswoman kept the sick lambs indoors.
items.exampleCN: 女牧人把病羔留在室内。

definition_en: passed from parents to offspring through genes, or transmitted by legal succession from one generation to the next
core_image: 家族相册里，几代人的手形几乎一模一样，连指节的弯度都对得上
scene: 家族相册里，几代人的手形几乎一模一样。A hereditary trait ran through every generation of the family.
sceneCN: 这里 hereditary 指「由上一代经遗传传下来的」（第 1 个义项：经基因传递的）；句意为一种遗传性状贯穿了这个家族的每一代。可辨识物件：相册、放大的手部照片、家谱线、铅笔标记。

derivatives.zh: 可继承的财产（法律用语）

senses.title: Passed through genes
senses.definition: transmitted from parents to offspring through genetic material
senses.definitionCN: 通过遗传物质由亲代传给子代
senses.example: Hereditary deafness runs in that family.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传性耳聋在那个家族中代代出现。
senses.why: The adjective describes a trait whose cause travels in the genes, so it names the route rather than the illness itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词描述病因随基因传递的性状，因此命名的是传递路径，而非疾病本身。

senses.title: Inherited from ancestors
senses.definition: received from an ancestor rather than acquired in one's own lifetime
senses.definitionCN: 从祖先处承接，而非在本人一生中获得
senses.example: The tendency is partly hereditary.
senses.exampleCN: 这种倾向有一部分是遗传的。
senses.why: The word can soften a claim: partly hereditary means ancestry contributes without settling the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以缓和断言：部分遗传意味着祖先有贡献，但并不决定结果。

senses.title: Transmitted by succession
senses.definition: passed down by legal or customary succession rather than election
senses.definitionCN: 按法律或习俗世袭传递，而非经选举
senses.example: The duke held a hereditary seat in the old assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 公爵在旧议会中拥有一个世袭席位。
senses.why: Law uses the same adjective for offices because a seat can pass to an heir just as an estate can.
senses.whyCN: 法律用同一个形容词描述职位，因为席位也能像产业一样传给继承人。

senses.title: Of hereditary monarchy
senses.definition: describing a system in which the head of state succeeds by birth
senses.definitionCN: 描述国家元首按出生顺序继位的制度
senses.example: The country replaced hereditary rule with elections.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家用选举取代了世袭统治。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to institutions, not only to bodies, when rule itself is handed down.
senses.whyCN: 当统治权本身被传下时，这个形容词也附着于制度，而不只是身体。

senses.title: Of hereditary material
senses.definition: relating to the material that carries genes from one cell to the next
senses.definitionCN: 与把基因从一代细胞带到下一代细胞的物质相关
senses.example: Hereditary material is copied into every cell.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传物质被复制进每一个细胞。
senses.why: In biology the adjective can modify the carrier as well as the trait, which is why hereditary material is a fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 在生物学中，这个形容词既能修饰性状，也能修饰载体，因此「遗传物质」成为固定搭配。

senses.title: Of a hereditary predisposition
senses.definition: describing an inherited tendency that raises risk without causing the condition alone
senses.definitionCN: 描述提高风险但并不单独致病的遗传倾向
senses.example: A hereditary predisposition does not guarantee illness.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传易感性并不保证一定患病。
senses.why: The word separates inheritance from inevitability: a predisposition is a loaded starting point, not a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「遗传」与「必然」分开：易感性是一个有负载的起点，而不是判决。

senses.title: Legally inheritable
senses.definition: able to pass to an heir under the law
senses.definitionCN: 依法可以传给继承人
senses.example: The estate was hereditary and could not be sold.
senses.exampleCN: 这份产业属于可继承财产，不能出售。
senses.why: Property law uses the adjective for land and rights that must descend rather than be traded freely.
senses.whyCN: 财产法用这个形容词描述必须下传、不能自由买卖的土地与权利。

senses.title: Carried down from the past
senses.definition: describing an attitude or conflict handed down so long that it seems inborn
senses.definitionCN: 描述传得太久、仿佛天生的态度或冲突
senses.example: The two villages were hereditary enemies.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个村子是世代相传的仇敌。
senses.why: The metaphor treats hostility as an estate: children receive a quarrel they never chose.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻把敌意当作产业：孩子们接收了一场他们从未选择的争吵。

intro.en: Hereditary comes from Latin hereditarius 'of an inheritance', from hereditas 'inheritance', from heres (hered-) 'heir'.
intro.cn: hereditary 来自拉丁 hereditarius「继承的」，再上溯 hereditas「继承」与 heres（hered-）「继承人」。

items.en: Heres (genitive heredis) meant 'heir'. Its deeper origin is not established; links to other Indo-European words are hypotheses, and any PIE form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: heres（属格 heredis）意为「继承人」。其更深来源未得到确证；与其他印欧语词的联系只是假说，任何原始印欧语形式均属重构。

items.en: Hereditarius 'of an inheritance' was formed from hereditas; the adjective suffix -arius marks belonging or relation.
items.cn: hereditarius「继承的」由 hereditas 构成；形容词后缀 -arius 表示归属或关系。

items.en: English took hereditary from Latin or French in the fifteenth or sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在 15 或 16 世纪从拉丁语或法语借入 hereditary；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The legal sense survives in hereditary titles and hereditary peers, where office passes by birth rather than election.
items.cn: 法律义残存于世袭头衔与世袭贵族，其职位按出生而非选举传递。

items.en: The biological sense developed in the nineteenth century, when heredity became a research subject and traits were traced through families.
items.cn: 生物学义在 19 世纪发展起来，当时遗传成为研究课题，性状被沿家族追踪。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): heres has no established pre-Latin etymology, and the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：heres 没有已确立的拉丁语之前词源，英语首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same hered- family that differ in grammar or nuance; group two holds adjectives that also describe what is present from birth or runs in families.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 hered- 词族、但语法角色或侧重不同的词；第二组是同样描述「出生即有」或「家族中常见」的形容词。

entries.definition: The process or system of transmission; hereditary is the adjective describing what is transmitted.
entries.definitionCN: 指传递过程或系统；hereditary 是描述被传递之物的形容词。

entries.definition: Able to be inherited, often used of traits or property; hereditary describes the actual transmission or legal status.
entries.definitionCN: 指能够被继承，常用于性状或财产；hereditary 描述实际的传递或法律地位。

entries.definition: A legal term for inheritable property; it is a noun of things, not a trait.
entries.definitionCN: 指可继承财产的法律术语；它是事物名词，不是性状。

entries.definition: The adverb form; it describes how something is transmitted rather than what it is.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式；描述传递方式，而非事物本身。

entries.definition: The ordinary participle from inherit; hereditary is the fixed adjective, especially in biology and law.
entries.definitionCN: inherit 的普通分词；hereditary 是固定形容词，尤用于生物学与法律。

entries.definition: Present at birth; a congenital condition may arise during development and need not be hereditary.
entries.definitionCN: 指出生时即存在；先天状况可能在发育中形成，未必是遗传的。

entries.definition: Occurring in a family more often than chance; familial does not prove a genetic cause.
entries.definitionCN: 指在家族中发生率高于偶然；familial 并不证明存在遗传原因。

entries.definition: The broad modern adjective; hereditary emphasises transmission from ancestors, genetic emphasises the genes themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 宽泛的现代形容词；hereditary 强调从祖先传递，genetic 强调基因本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: heres 'heir' + -ary: belonging to an inheritance.
normal.cn: heres「继承人」+ -ary：属于继承的。

normal.en: The family runs hereditary, heredity, hereditarily and hereditament.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 hereditary、heredity、hereditarily 与 hereditament。

normal.en: Law fixes hereditary peer and hereditary title; biology fixes hereditary disease.
normal.cn: 法律固定搭配世袭贵族、世袭头衔；生物学固定搭配遗传性疾病。

normal.en: Hereditary peer describes a seat, not a gene.
normal.cn: 世袭贵族描述的是席位，不是基因。

normal.en: A hereditary predisposition raises risk without deciding the outcome.
normal.cn: 遗传易感性提高风险，却不决定结果。

abstract.en: Picture a seal stamped on every generation of a document.
abstract.cn: 想象每一代文件上都盖着同一枚印章。

abstract.en: Picture a tune learned before birth and never questioned.
abstract.cn: 想象一支在出生前就学会、从不被质疑的曲子。

abstract.en: Picture a title that comes with the furniture, not with a vote.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头衔随家具而来，而不是随选票而来。

examples.en: The condition is hereditary, though not everyone who carries the gene falls ill.
examples.cn: 这种病是遗传的，但并非每个携带该基因的人都会发病。

examples.en: Hereditary peers lost their voting rights in the reform.
examples.cn: 世袭贵族在改革中失去了投票权。

examples.en: The museum refused to sell the hereditary collection.
examples.cn: 博物馆拒绝出售这批世袭收藏。

dict_mnemonic.text: hered（继承人）+ itary（形容词尾）——与继承人相关的 → 世袭的、遗传的。

root: 拉丁 hereditarius「继承的」← hereditas「继承」← heres（hered-）「继承人」；heres 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a stamp that keeps reappearing: in genes, in ancestry, in offices, in monarchy, in cellular material, in risk, in property law and finally in inherited hostility.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一枚反复出现的印章展开：出现在基因、祖先、职位、君主制、细胞物质、风险、财产法，最后出现在沿袭的敌意中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same hand shape appearing in photograph after photograph.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一手形在一张又一张照片中反复出现。

branches.en: GENETIC AND ANCESTRAL: a trait travels through genes and is received from ancestors.
branches.cn: 遗传与祖先：性状经基因传递，并从祖先处承接。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND RISK: the carrier itself, and an inherited tendency that only raises risk.
branches.cn: 物质与风险：载体本身，以及只提高风险的遗传倾向。

branches.en: OFFICE AND RULE: seats and crowns pass by birth rather than election.
branches.cn: 职位与统治：席位与王冠按出生而非选举传递。

branches.en: PROPERTY LAW: land and rights that must descend to heirs.
branches.cn: 财产法：必须下传给继承人的土地与权利。

branches.en: INHERITED HOSTILITY: an old quarrel arrives like an estate.
branches.cn: 沿袭的敌意：旧日争吵像产业一样被接收。

intro.en: Hereditary is an adjective built on the Latin hered- stem plus a suffix, and the same stem builds a legal and biological family.
intro.cn: hereditary 是由拉丁 hered- 词干加后缀构成的形容词，同一词干还构成法律与生物词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres (hered-) gives hereditas, hereditarius, hereditary, heredity and inherit; -arius marks belonging.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 heres（hered-）衍生 hereditas、hereditarius、hereditary、heredity 与 inherit；-arius 标记归属关系。

items.example: The stem names the person who receives.
Hereditas named the estate and the relation together.
items.exampleCN: hereditas 同时命名产业与关系。

items.example: The adjective added -arius to the stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在词干后加 -arius。

items.example: The suffix turns the stem into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词干变成描述词。
这一性状以遗传方式传递。
契据列明了每一项可继承财产。

items.example: The debate drew both hereditarians and environmentalists.
items.exampleCN: 这场争论吸引了遗传论者与环境论者。

definition_en: the transmission of traits from parents to offspring, or the set of inherited characteristics of an organism
core_image: 同一对父母养大的子女，身高与性格却各有差别，差别像从看不见的账本里带出来的
scene: 同一对父母养大的子女，身高与性格却各有差别。Researchers separate the effects of heredity from those of upbringing.
sceneCN: 这里 heredity 指「亲代把性状传给子代的生物过程」（第 1 个义项：性状的遗传传递）；句意为研究者把遗传的影响与养育的影响分开。可辨识物件：并排的身高尺、两张性格记录表、家谱图、双栏表格。

senses.title: Transmission of traits
senses.definition: the passing of characteristics from parents to offspring
senses.definitionCN: 特征由亲代传给子代
senses.example: Heredity explains why siblings resemble their parents.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传解释了为什么兄弟姐妹像他们的父母。
senses.why: The word names the process itself, not the genes that carry it, which is why it pairs naturally with environment.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名过程本身，而非承载它的基因，因此天然与「环境」配对。

senses.title: An organism's inherited constitution
senses.definition: the total set of inherited characteristics of an organism
senses.definitionCN: 一个生物体所继承的全部特征
senses.example: Heredity and environment interact in development.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传与环境在发育中相互作用。
senses.why: The process sense and the constitution sense share a form: what is transmitted becomes what an organism carries.
senses.whyCN: 过程义与组成义共用一词形：被传下的东西成为生物体所携带的东西。

senses.title: The study of inheritance
senses.definition: the field or subject concerned with transmission of traits
senses.definitionCN: 研究性状传递的领域或学科
senses.example: Heredity was studied long before genes were named.
senses.exampleCN: 早在基因被命名之前，人们就在研究遗传。
senses.why: The name of the process also names the subject that studies it, so heredity can stand for a field of inquiry.
senses.whyCN: 过程之名也命名研究它的学科，因此 heredity 可以指一个研究领域。

senses.title: Laws of heredity
senses.definition: the regular patterns by which traits appear in later generations
senses.definitionCN: 性状在后代中出现的规律模式
senses.example: Mendel's laws of heredity describe the ratios of traits.
senses.exampleCN: 孟德尔的遗传规律描述了性状的比例。
senses.why: Once patterns were counted, heredity could be spoken of as having laws rather than merely effects.
senses.whyCN: 一旦模式可以被计数，遗传就可以被说成有规律，而不只是有效应。

senses.title: Heredity versus environment
senses.definition: the relative contribution of inherited and environmental factors
senses.definitionCN: 遗传因素与环境因素的相对贡献
senses.example: The debate over heredity and environment has softened.
senses.exampleCN: 关于遗传与环境的争论已经缓和。
senses.why: The word became a pole in a debate, so heredity often appears opposite environment rather than alone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词成了争论中的一极，因此 heredity 常与 environment 相对出现，而非单独使用。

senses.title: Heredity as a biological force
senses.definition: the influence of inherited factors on development and behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 遗传因素对发育与行为的影响
senses.example: Heredity sets limits that nutrition can only partly shift.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传设定了界限，营养只能部分改变。
senses.why: When treated as a force, heredity explains the range of possible development rather than a single fixed result.
senses.whyCN: 当被当作一种力量时，遗传解释的是发育的可能范围，而非单一固定结果。

senses.title: Heredity in breeding
senses.definition: the transmission that breeders rely on when fixing traits
senses.definitionCN: 育种者固定性状时所依赖的传递
senses.example: Heredity determines which traits a breeder can fix.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传决定育种者能固定哪些性状。
senses.why: Breeders work with heredity as a practical constraint: some traits can be fixed, others cannot.
senses.whyCN: 育种者把遗传当作实际限制来工作：有些性状可以固定，有些不能。

senses.title: Archaic legal inheritance
senses.definition: the old sense of inheriting property or a right
senses.definitionCN: 继承财产或权利的旧义
senses.example: In older legal writing, heredity meant the right to inherit.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的法律文本中，heredity 指继承权。
senses.why: The legal sense is the oldest layer of the word, preserved in older statutes rather than in modern biology.
senses.whyCN: 法律义是这个词最古老的层次，保存在较早的法条中，而非现代生物学中。

intro.en: Heredity was borrowed from Latin hereditas 'inheritance, heirship', from heres (hered-) 'heir'.
intro.cn: heredity 直接借自拉丁 hereditas「继承、继承权」，其词干为 heres（hered-）「继承人」。

items.en: Heres (genitive heredis) meant 'heir'. Its deeper origin is not established; related forms in other Indo-European languages are hypotheses, and any PIE form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: heres（属格 heredis）意为「继承人」。其更深来源未得到确证；其他印欧语中的相关形式只是假说，任何原始印欧语形式均属重构。

items.en: Hereditas meant 'inheritance, heirship'; English heredity was borrowed directly from this Latin noun rather than through French.
items.cn: hereditas 意为「继承、继承权」；英语 heredity 直接借自这个拉丁名词，而非经法语。

items.en: The word appears in English by the sixteenth century with the legal sense 'inheritance'; the exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在 16 世纪已以「继承」的法律义出现在英语中；确切的最早书证不确定。

items.en: In the nineteenth century heredity was reshaped into the biological term for the transmission of traits, as breeding and cell theory advanced.
items.cn: 19 世纪，随着育种与细胞理论进展，heredity 被重塑为性状传递的生物学术语。

items.en: Twentieth-century genetics narrowed heredity to the transmission itself, distinct from the genes that carry it.
items.cn: 20 世纪的遗传学把 heredity 收窄为传递过程本身，与承载它的基因区分开。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the pre-Latin origin of heres is unsettled, and the shift from legal to biological use is not sharply dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：heres 的拉丁语之前来源未有定论，从法律义到生物学义的转变也没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one separates heredity from same-root words with different grammar; group two separates it from the words for inheritance, lineage and the science of genes.
note.cn: 第一组把 heredity 与同根但语法角色不同的词分开；第二组把它与继承、世系、基因科学相关词区分。

entries.definition: The adjective describing what is transmitted; heredity is the process or constitution itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述被传递之物的形容词；heredity 是过程或组成本身。

entries.definition: What is handed down, especially culture or family property; it is not the biological process.
entries.definitionCN: 指被传下的东西，尤其是文化或家族财产；不是生物过程。

entries.definition: Able to be inherited; the word describes a possibility, while heredity names the actual transmission.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被继承；描述可能性，而 heredity 命名实际传递。

entries.definition: A person or doctrine stressing heredity as a cause of differences; it belongs to debate rather than biology alone.
entries.definitionCN: 强调遗传是差异原因的人或学说；属于争论语境，而非单纯生物学。

entries.definition: A broader word covering legal property and biological transmission; heredity is the biological process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 较宽泛的词，涵盖法定财产与生物传递；heredity 是生物过程本身。

entries.definition: The modern science of genes; heredity names the transmission that genetics explains.
entries.definitionCN: 研究基因的现代科学；heredity 命名遗传学所要解释的传递。

entries.definition: Ancestry or lineage, especially as a line of descent; heredity is the mechanism, descent is the line.
entries.definitionCN: 指血统或世系，尤指一条下传的线；heredity 是机制，descent 是那条线。

entries.definition: A neutral term for passing anything from one generation to the next, biological or not.
entries.definitionCN: 中性词，指把任何东西传给下一代，不论是否生物性的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: heres 'heir' + -ity: the state of being inherited.
normal.cn: heres「继承人」+ -ity：被继承的状态。

normal.en: The family runs heredity, hereditary, hereditarily and hereditarian.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 heredity、hereditary、hereditarily 与 hereditarian。

normal.en: The fixed pair is heredity and environment.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是遗传与环境。

normal.en: Laws of heredity were counted before genes were named.
normal.cn: 在基因被命名之前，遗传规律就已被计数。

normal.en: Modern genetics separates heredity from the genes that carry it.
normal.cn: 现代遗传学把遗传过程与承载它的基因分开。

abstract.en: Picture an invisible ledger that each child receives with a few entries already filled in.
abstract.cn: 想象每个孩子都收到一本看不见的账本，上面已写好几笔。

abstract.en: Picture two seeds from one pod landing in different soils.
abstract.cn: 想象同一豆荚里的两粒种子落在不同的土里。

abstract.en: Picture a hand of cards dealt before anyone chooses how to play.
abstract.cn: 想象一手牌在任何人决定怎么打之前就已发好。

examples.en: Heredity alone does not explain the difference between the twins.
examples.cn: 单靠遗传解释不了这对双胞胎的差异。

examples.en: Breeders rely on heredity when they select for a fixed coat colour.
examples.cn: 育种者选育固定毛色时依赖遗传。

examples.en: The old statute used heredity in the sense of a right to inherit.
examples.cn: 旧法规用 heredity 指继承权。

dict_mnemonic.text: hered（继承人）+ ity（名词尾）——继承人接到的东西 → 遗传；旧义才是「继承」。

root: 拉丁 hereditas「继承、继承权」← heres（hered-）「继承人」；heres 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a current running through generations: the process, the constitution it produces, the study of it, its laws, its debate with environment, its force, its use in breeding and its old legal sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一股穿越世代的电流展开：传递过程、由此形成的组成、对它的研究、它的规律、它与环境的争论、它的力量、它在育种中的用途，以及旧时的法律义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible ledger handed to each child with a few entries already filled in.
core.cn: 核心意象：每个孩子都收到一本看不见的账本，上面已写好几笔。

branches.en: PROCESS AND FORCE: transmission itself, and the influence it exerts on development.
branches.cn: 过程与力量：传递本身，以及它对发育施加的影响。

branches.en: CONSTITUTION AND BREEDING: what an organism carries, and what a breeder can fix.
branches.cn: 组成与育种：生物体携带什么，育种者能固定什么。

branches.en: STUDY: the field that examines transmission before and after genes were named.
branches.cn: 研究：在基因被命名前后考察传递的领域。

branches.en: LAWS AND DEBATE: counted ratios, and the argument with environment.
branches.cn: 规律与争论：可计数的比例，以及与环境的论战。

branches.en: OLD LAW: the archaic sense of a right to inherit property.
branches.cn: 旧法律：继承财产之权利的古老义。

intro.en: Heredity is a Latin noun built on the hered- stem; the same stem forms the legal and biological words around it.
intro.cn: heredity 是建立在 hered- 词干上的拉丁名词；同一词干构成周围的法律与生物词。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres (hered-) gives hereditas, hereditarius, heredity, hereditary and inherit; no prefix is involved in heredity itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 heres（hered-）衍生 hereditas、hereditarius、heredity、hereditary 与 inherit；heredity 本身不含前缀。

items.example: The stem names the person who receives.
Hereditas is the direct source of heredity.
items.exampleCN: hereditas 是 heredity 的直接来源。
这个形容词提供了 hereditary。

items.example: The suffix turns the stem into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词干变成状态名词。
这一性状以遗传方式传递。
继承人在契据上签了字。

latinEntries.meaning: to inherit, leave as an inheritance

definition_zh: 遗产；继承的财产；世代相传的传统与文化；出身与天赋权利；历史遗迹与自然遗产
definition_en: property, traditions or culture passed down from earlier generations
core_image: 阁楼上那台旧织机蒙着布，几代人搬了几次家都没舍得丢
scene: 阁楼上那台旧织机蒙着布，几代人搬了几次家都没舍得丢，The family keeps the loom as part of its heritage.
sceneCN: 这里 heritage 指「从先辈继承下来、代代保留的财物」（第 1 个义项：继承的财产）；句意为这家人把那台织机当作遗产的一部分保留下来。图中可辨识物件：蒙布的织机、木楼梯、旧箱子、系着标签的钥匙。

pos.zh: 遗产；继承的财产；世代相传的传统与文化；历史遗迹

senses.title: Property inherited from ancestors
senses.definition: money, land or objects received from a predecessor, especially within a family
senses.definitionCN: 从前人、尤指家族成员那里接受的金钱、土地或物件
senses.example: The family keeps the loom as part of its heritage.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人把那台织机当作遗产的一部分保留下来。
senses.why: The oldest sense is legal and material: heritage is what passes to an heir when an owner dies.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是法律与物质上的：遗产是业主去世后传给继承人的东西。

senses.title: Traditions and values passed down
senses.titleCN: 世代相传的传统与价值观
senses.definition: customs, beliefs, stories and skills handed from one generation to the next
senses.definitionCN: 一代代传下的习俗、信念、故事与技艺
senses.example: The village's heritage lives in its songs more than in its buildings.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄的遗产更多活在歌谣里，而不是建筑里。
senses.why: The legal handover is reused for culture: what is passed down may be a way of doing things rather than a deed.
senses.whyCN: 法律上的交接被挪用到文化上：传下来的可能是做事的方式，而不是一纸契据。

senses.title: Birthright and inherited status
senses.titleCN: 与生俱来的权利与继承的身份
senses.definition: the rights, rank or identity one holds by birth or family line
senses.definitionCN: 因出生或家族世系而拥有的权利、等级或身份
senses.example: She wears the ring as a sign of her heritage, not of her wealth.
senses.exampleCN: 她戴这枚戒指，表示的是她的出身，而不是财富。
senses.why: Heritage can be intangible in a social sense: a name or a rank arrives without any object changing hands.
senses.whyCN: 遗产在社会意义上可以是无形的：一个姓氏或一个等级到手时，并没有任何物件易手。

senses.title: Built heritage
senses.definition: historic buildings, monuments and townscapes valued as a collective inheritance
senses.definitionCN: 被当作集体继承物而珍视的历史建筑、纪念物与城镇景观
senses.example: The trust lists the mill as built heritage and forbids its demolition.
senses.exampleCN: 该信托机构把磨坊列为建筑遗产，禁止拆除。
senses.why: When a whole society inherits a building, the private word becomes public and legal.
senses.whyCN: 当整个社会继承一栋建筑，这个私人词汇就变成公共与法律用语。

senses.title: Natural heritage
senses.definition: landscapes, habitats and species treated as an inheritance worth protecting
senses.definitionCN: 被当作值得保护的继承物来对待的景观、栖息地与物种
senses.example: The valley's natural heritage includes the old orchard varieties.
senses.exampleCN: 这座山谷的自然遗产包括那些古老的果树品种。
senses.why: Heritage can be extended to what no human made: a landscape is inherited too, and can be lost like a building.
senses.whyCN: 遗产可以扩展到并非人造之物：一片景观也是继承来的，也会像建筑一样失去。

senses.title: The roots that shape identity
senses.definition: the inherited culture through which a person or group understands who they are
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或群体借以理解自身身份来源的继承文化
senses.example: He returned to the old quarter to recover a heritage he had never learned.
senses.exampleCN: 他回到老城区，想找回一份自己从未学过的遗产。
senses.why: Heritage answers the question where do I come from, so it becomes a resource for identity rather than a possession.
senses.whyCN: 遗产回答「我从哪里来」，因此它成为认同的资源，而非一件所有物。

senses.title: Heritage as tourism and industry
senses.titleCN: 作为旅游与产业的遗产
senses.definition: inherited places and traditions packaged and sold as visitor attractions
senses.definitionCN: 被包装并作为游客吸引物出售的继承场所与传统
senses.example: The heritage industry restored the harbour and then raised the ticket price.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产产业修复了港口，随后提高了票价。
senses.why: A public inheritance needs money to survive, and selling access to it creates a business with its own interests.
senses.whyCN: 公共继承物需要钱才能存活，而出售接近它的权利，就造出一个有自身利益的产业。

senses.title: The legacy of a movement or era
senses.titleCN: 一场运动或一个时代的遗泽
senses.definition: the achievements or consequences that later people receive from an earlier movement or period
senses.definitionCN: 后来者从较早的运动或时期那里继承的成就或后果
senses.example: Public libraries are part of the heritage of the reform movement.
senses.exampleCN: 公共图书馆是那场改革运动的遗泽之一。
senses.why: The family image widens one last time: a generation can inherit not only from relatives but from a struggle it never joined.
senses.whyCN: 家族的意象最后一次被放宽：一代人不仅可以从亲属那里继承，也可以从一场自己未曾参与的抗争中继承。

intro.en: Heritage comes through Old French from Late Latin hereditare, to inherit, built on Latin heres, heir. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: heritage 经古法语来自晚期拉丁语 hereditare「继承」，后者由拉丁语 heres「继承人」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Heres meant heir. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and it is not securely linked to another Latin root.
items.cn: heres 意为「继承人」。它更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠地联系到另一个拉丁词根。

items.en: Hereditare, to inherit or to leave by will, was formed on the hered- stem of heres and its noun hereditas, inheritance.
items.cn: hereditare 意为「继承或按遗嘱留下」，由 heres 的词干 hered- 及其名词 hereditas「继承」构成。

items.en: Old French eritage named an inherited estate; the h was restored in English spelling under Latin influence.
items.cn: 古法语 eritage 指继承的产业；英语拼写受拉丁语影响又补回了 h。

items.en: Middle English heritage first meant inherited property and the right to inherit it.
items.cn: 中古英语 heritage 最初指继承的财产以及继承它的权利。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word widened from private property to the shared past of a people, and later to buildings and landscapes.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，这个词从私人财产扩展到民族共有的过去，后来又扩展到建筑与景观。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of the cultural sense is not securely dated, and the origin of heres remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：文化义在英语中的最早使用没有确切年代；heres 的来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds words from the heir root that differ in word class; the second holds near synonyms for what is passed down.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「继承人」词根、但词性不同的词；第二组是表示「传下之物」的近义词。

entries.definition: To receive property, traits or traditions from a predecessor; heritage is the noun for what is received.
entries.definitionCN: 从前人那里接受财产、性状或传统；heritage 是表示所接受之物的名词。

entries.definition: The property or traits received, especially in law or genetics; heritage is broader and often cultural.
entries.definitionCN: 所接受的财产或性状，尤其在法律或遗传学中；heritage 更宽，常指文化。

entries.definition: Passed from parent to child by blood or legal line; it describes the route of transmission, not the thing transmitted.
entries.definitionCN: 由血统或法定世系从父母传给子女；它描述传递路径，而非传递之物。

entries.definition: Capable of being inherited, used of property or traits; it is a technical adjective, not the noun heritage.
entries.definitionCN: 可被继承的，用于财产或性状；它是技术性形容词，不是名词 heritage。

entries.definition: Something handed down, often with a personal or historical tone; heritage is more collective and more official.
entries.definitionCN: 前人留下之物，常带个人或历史语气；heritage 更集体、更官方。

entries.definition: An inheritance from ancestors, especially national or religious property; it is more formal and more legal than heritage.
entries.definitionCN: 祖先传下的遗产，尤指国家或宗教财产；比 heritage 更正式、更法律化。

entries.definition: A custom or belief passed down by repeated practice; it is one kind of heritage, not its whole body.
entries.definitionCN: 通过反复实践传下的习俗或信念；它是遗产的一种，而非全部。

entries.definition: A right or property one holds from birth; it stresses entitlement, while heritage stresses the handover.
entries.definitionCN: 因出生而拥有的权利或财产；它强调应得资格，而 heritage 强调交接。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real heir root, the real family and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「继承人」词根、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: heritage shares the hered- stem with inherit and inheritance: all point to a handover to an heir.
normal.cn: heritage 与 inherit（继承）、inheritance（继承、遗产）共享 hered- 词干：都指向把东西交给继承人。

normal.en: The family runs heritage, inherit, inheritance, hereditary, heritable and inheritor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 heritage（遗产）、inherit（继承）、inheritance（继承、遗产）、hereditary（世袭的）、heritable（可继承的）、inheritor（继承人）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: national heritage, world heritage, heritage site, heritage industry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：国家遗产、世界遗产、遗产地、遗产产业。

normal.en: The word moved from a private will to a public past, then to buildings and landscapes.
normal.cn: 这个词从一份私人遗嘱移到公共的过去，再移到建筑与景观。

normal.en: A useful contrast: inheritance is legal and technical, while heritage is cultural and collective.
normal.cn: 有用的对照：inheritance 是法律与技术用语，而 heritage 是文化与集体用语。

abstract.en: Picture a trunk in an attic, labelled not with a name but with a generation.
abstract.cn: 想象阁楼上的一只箱子，标签上写的不是名字，而是一代人。

abstract.en: Picture a key that opens a door its owner has never seen.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙，打开一扇它的主人从未见过的门。

abstract.en: Picture a river that carries the silt of fields no living farmer ploughed.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河，载着在世农夫从未犁过的田地的泥沙。

examples.en: The museum treats the dialect recordings as heritage rather than as data.
examples.cn: 博物馆把方言录音当作遗产，而不是数据。

examples.en: World heritage status brought money and also brought crowds.
examples.cn: 世界遗产地位带来了钱，也带来了人潮。

examples.en: Heritage is not only what survives; it is what someone chooses to hand on.
examples.cn: 遗产不只是幸存下来的东西；它是有人选择传下去的东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喝瑞替吉」听成「喝了记得」——先辈留下的老屋与歌谣，喝了水也要记得，就是遗产。

root: 经古法语 eritage 来自晚期拉丁语 hereditare「继承」，后者由拉丁语 heres「继承人」及其词干 hered- 构成，并与 hereditas「继承」同族。heres 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one handover: property, traditions, status, built places, natural places, identity, tourism and finally the legacy of a movement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次交接展开：财产、传统、身份、建筑、自然场所、认同、旅游，最后是一场运动的遗泽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object passed from a dying hand to a living one, with no receipt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件东西从将逝的手交到活着的手里，没有收据。

branches.en: PRIVATE INHERITANCE: property and status pass to an heir, whether or not any object changes hands.
branches.cn: 私人继承：财产与身份传给继承人，无论是否有物件易手。

branches.en: CULTURE: songs, skills and beliefs are inherited like an estate.
branches.cn: 文化：歌谣、技艺与信念像产业一样被继承。

branches.en: BUILT: a whole society becomes the heir of a building.
branches.cn: 建筑：整个社会成为一栋建筑的继承人。

branches.en: NATURAL: landscapes are inherited too and can be lost like buildings.

definition_zh: 冬眠；越冬休眠状态；（计算机）休眠
definition_en: a state in which an animal passes the winter with greatly lowered body temperature and metabolism
core_image: 洞穴深处一只动物蜷成一团，呼吸慢到几乎听不见，洞口外面覆着厚雪
scene: 洞穴深处，一只蝙蝠把身体缩成一团，心跳降到每分钟几次，整个冬天几乎不动。A deep hibernation lets the bat survive months without food.
sceneCN: 这里 hibernation 指「动物以极低代谢状态度过整个冬天的休眠」（第 1 个义项：越冬低代谢休眠状态）；句意为深度冬眠让这只蝙蝠在没有食物的数月里存活。图中可辨识物件：倒挂的蝙蝠、岩壁凹处、呼出的白气、洞口的雪。

pos.zh: 冬眠；越冬休眠（不可数；指一次具体的冬眠期时可数，复数 hibernations）

forms.label: 复数（指多次或多种冬眠）

derivatives.zh: hibernate（基础动词；hibernation 由 hibernate + -ion 动作名词后缀构成）→ 以低代谢状态过冬
hibernate + -or（施动者后缀）→ 进行冬眠的动物
hibernare + -aculum（拉丁「场所」后缀）→ 越冬的巢、穴或越冬芽

senses.title: The winter dormant state
senses.titleCN: 动物越冬的低代谢休眠状态
senses.definition: the condition in which an animal's body temperature, heart rate and metabolism fall sharply for the winter
senses.definitionCN: 动物体温、心率与代谢在冬季大幅下降的状态
senses.example: A deep hibernation lets the bat survive months without food.
senses.exampleCN: 深度冬眠让这只蝙蝠在没有食物的数月里存活。
senses.why: Latin hibernare meant 'to pass the winter', so the noun first names the whole wintering, then the physiological state that makes it possible.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 hibernare 意为「过冬」，因此这个名词先指整个越冬过程，再指使越冬成为可能的生理状态。

senses.title: The span of months spent dormant
senses.definition: the period from the onset of dormancy to the spring awakening
senses.definitionCN: 从进入休眠到春天苏醒之间的这段时间
senses.example: Their hibernation lasts from the first hard frost to the thaw.
senses.exampleCN: 它们的冬眠从第一场严霜持续到解冻。
senses.why: A state and the time it fills are named by the same noun, so hibernation can answer the question 'how long?'.
senses.whyCN: 状态与状态所占的时间用同一个名词表达，因此 hibernation 也能回答「多久」。

senses.title: The physiological mechanism behind it
senses.definition: the controlled drop in temperature, breathing and heartbeat that keeps the body alive on stored fat
senses.definitionCN: 体温、呼吸与心跳的受控下降，使身体靠储存的脂肪维持生命
senses.example: Hibernation slows the heart to a few beats a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 冬眠把心跳降到每分钟几次。
senses.why: The word can name the mechanism rather than the season because the interesting part is how the body survives the cold.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以指机制而非季节，因为真正引人注意的是身体如何在寒冷中活下来。

senses.title: Winter dormancy in a particular group
senses.definition: the specific form of winter rest found in bats, insects, snakes or other named animals
senses.definitionCN: 蝙蝠、昆虫、蛇等特定动物所具有的那一种越冬休眠
senses.example: Insect hibernation may begin long before the first snow.
senses.exampleCN: 昆虫的冬眠可能在第一场雪之前很久就开始。
senses.why: Because each group does it differently, the noun is often paired with the animal's name to mark a distinct pattern.
senses.whyCN: 因为各类群做法不同，这个名词常与动物名连用，标出一种特定的模式。

senses.title: Suspending a computer to disk
senses.titleCN: 计算机把内存写入磁盘的休眠
senses.definition: the power state in which a computer writes its memory to disk and shuts down completely until switched on again
senses.definitionCN: 计算机把内存内容写入磁盘并完全断电，直到再次开机才恢复的电源状态
senses.example: The laptop's hibernation saves the open files to disk before the battery dies.
senses.exampleCN: 笔记本的休眠在电池耗尽前把打开的文件存入磁盘。
senses.why: The machine imitates the animal: activity stops, the body is preserved in a safe place, and waking is still possible.
senses.whyCN: 机器模仿动物：活动停止，内容被保存在安全处，之后仍能醒来。

senses.title: Induced torpor for long spaceflight
senses.titleCN: 长期太空飞行中的人为休眠设想
senses.definition: the proposed medical state in which astronauts would be cooled and slowed to cut food, water and oxygen needs
senses.definitionCN: 设想中的医学状态：让航天员降温减速，以减少食物、水与氧气需求
senses.example: Engineers study hibernation as a way to cut the supplies needed for a Mars mission.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师研究冬眠，把它作为减少火星任务补给需求的办法。
senses.why: Space medicine borrows the animal strategy because mass is expensive and months of cruising are long.
senses.whyCN: 航天医学借用动物的策略，因为载荷重量昂贵，而数月巡航又太漫长。

senses.title: A period of institutional stagnation
senses.titleCN: 组织或市场的长期蛰伏
senses.definition: a figurative stretch in which a company, market or project stops growing and waits for better conditions
senses.definitionCN: 公司、市场或项目停止成长、等待时机好转的比喻性停滞期
senses.example: The industry's hibernation ended when demand returned.
senses.exampleCN: 需求回升后，这个行业的蛰伏期结束了。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the shape of the biological state: low activity, preserved resources, eventual waking.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了生物状态的外形：低活动、保住资源、最终醒来。

senses.title: Therapeutic cooling of a patient
senses.titleCN: 对病人的治疗性低温处理
senses.definition: a controlled medical cooling used to protect the brain or organs after injury or during long surgery
senses.definitionCN: 在损伤之后或长时间手术中，用受控降温保护大脑或器官的医疗手段
senses.example: Doctors are testing induced hibernation to protect tissue during long operations.
senses.exampleCN: 医生正在试验诱导性休眠，以在长时间手术中保护组织。
senses.why: The clinical sense borrows the name because cooling slows demand for oxygen in tissue, as it does in a hibernating animal.
senses.whyCN: 临床义借用这个名称，因为降温会像冬眠动物那样降低组织对氧的需求。

intro.en: Hibernation comes from Latin hibernare 'to pass the winter', a verb built on hibernus 'wintry' and hiems 'winter'. The noun entered English in the seventeenth century, first as a description of wintering and soon as a biological state.
intro.cn: hibernation 来自拉丁 hibernare「过冬」，该动词由 hibernus「冬天的」与 hiems「冬天」构成。这个名词在十七世纪进入英语，最初描述越冬，随后指生物学上的休眠状态。

items.en: Hiems was the ordinary Latin noun for winter. Its further origin is usually traced to a reconstructed Indo-European root for snow and winter, written with an asterisk because the form is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: hiems 是拉丁语中表示「冬天」的常用名词。其更早来源一般追溯到原始印欧语中表示雪与冬天的重构词根；因该形式是重构而非有文献佐证，学界用星号标出。

items.en: Hibernus meant 'wintry, of winter', an adjective derived from hiems. It survives in English hibernal, a formal word for winter things.
items.cn: hibernus 意为「冬天的、冬季的」，是由 hiems 派生的形容词，在英语中留下 hibernal 这一正式用词。

items.en: Hibernare meant 'to winter, to spend the winter'. In classical use it described soldiers wintering in camp; the biological sense of torpor is a later scientific narrowing.
items.cn: hibernare 意为「过冬、度过冬天」。古典用法指士兵在营地越冬；指生理性昏睡的生物学义是后来科学用法的收窄。

items.en: English took the noun in the 1660s, at first for the act of wintering and then for the dormant condition of animals. The precise first written date varies between sources.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪六十年代引入这个名词，先指越冬这件事，后指动物的休眠状态。各家记载的最早书面年代略有出入。

items.en: As physiology measured metabolism, the word was fixed to the state of lowered temperature, heart rate and oxygen use, distinguishing true hibernation from ordinary sleep.
items.cn: 随着生理学能够测量代谢，这个词被固定为体温、心率与耗氧下降的状态，从而与普通睡眠区分开来。

items.en: Computing borrowed the word in the late twentieth century for the power state that writes memory to disk and shuts the machine down.
items.cn: 计算技术在二十世纪后期借用这个词，指把内存写入磁盘并关机的电源状态。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same Latin winter family that are easily mixed up; group two holds other words for reduced biological activity.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「冬天」词族、容易混淆的形式；第二组是其他表示生物活动降低的词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'of winter', from hibernus; it describes the season, not the dormant state.
entries.definitionCN: 由 hibernus 来的形容词，意为「冬季的」，描述季节而非休眠状态。

entries.definition: The Latin word for winter quarters, used in biology for the shelter or bud in which an organism overwinters.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语「冬营」，生物学用来指生物越冬所在的巢穴或越冬芽。

entries.definition: The agent noun for an animal that hibernates, formed with -or just as in generator or oscillator.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行冬眠的动物的施动名词，与 generator、oscillator 一样由 -or 构成。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun; using it in place of hibernation changes the sentence from a state to an action.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词；用它替换 hibernation，句子就从状态变成动作。

entries.definition: A broad term for any temporary slowdown in growth or activity, including seeds and buds; hibernation is one winter form of it.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指生长或活动暂时减慢，包括种子与芽；冬眠是其中一种冬季形式。

entries.definition: A short-term drop in body temperature and activity, often nightly; hibernation is the long seasonal version.
entries.definitionCN: 体温与活动短时间下降，常按夜发生；冬眠是漫长的季节性版本。

entries.definition: The summer equivalent, passed through heat or drought rather than cold; the two words are seasonal opposites.
entries.definitionCN: 夏季对应形式，是在炎热或干旱中而非寒冷中度过；两词是季节上的对立面。

entries.definition: Surviving the winter by any strategy, including migration or active foraging; it does not require deep torpor.
entries.definitionCN: 以任何策略活过冬天，包括迁徙或照常觅食；不要求深度昏睡。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin hiems 'winter' plus hibernus 'wintry' gives hibernare 'to winter': winter turned into a verb.
normal.cn: 拉丁 hiems「冬天」加 hibernus「冬季的」得出 hibernare「过冬」：把冬天变成动词。

normal.en: The family runs hibernate, hibernation, hibernator, hibernaculum, hibernal, pre-hibernation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 hibernate、hibernation、hibernator、hibernaculum、hibernal、pre-hibernation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the state: enter hibernation, deep hibernation, arouse from hibernation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出状态：进入冬眠、深度冬眠、从冬眠中苏醒。

normal.en: The computer command hibernate uses the same picture: save the body, stop the clock, wake later.
normal.cn: 电脑的休眠命令用的是同一幅图：保存身体、停下时钟、日后再唤醒。

normal.en: Hibernation is seasonal, not nightly: torpor is the short version, hibernation the long one.
normal.cn: 冬眠是季节性的而非每夜的：昏睡是短版本，冬眠是长版本。

abstract.en: Picture a clock wound down but not broken, its hands parked until someone shakes it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只发条松开却未损坏的钟，指针停着，直到有人把它摇醒。

abstract.en: Picture a house closed for the winter with the water drained and the furniture under sheets.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋为过冬而封闭的房子，水排空了，家具盖着布。

abstract.en: Picture a seed of silence kept in a drawer until spring opens it.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒「沉默的种子」放在抽屉里，等春天把它打开。

examples.en: A deep hibernation lets the bat survive months without food.
examples.cn: 深度冬眠让这只蝙蝠在没有食物的数月里存活。

examples.en: Hibernation slows the heart to a few beats a minute.
examples.cn: 冬眠把心跳降到每分钟几次。

examples.en: The laptop's hibernation saves the open files to disk before the battery dies.
examples.cn: 笔记本的休眠在电池耗尽前把打开的文件存入磁盘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嗨，被窝」——天冷了钻进被窝长睡不醒 → 冬眠

root: 拉丁 hibernare「过冬」，由 hibernus「冬天的」构成，源于 hiems「冬天」；更早形式一般追溯到原始印欧语表示雪与冬天的重构词根（带星号的重构形式），确切音形存疑。英语 hibernate / hibernation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: life turns itself down to a minimum and waits. The gesture is biological first, then extends to machines, spaceflight, institutions and hospitals.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：生命把自己调到最低限度然后等待。这个动作先属于生物，再延伸到机器、航天、机构与医院。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curled body in a cold chamber, breathing almost unheard, snow at the entrance.
core.cn: 核心意象：寒冷洞穴里蜷成一团的身体，呼吸几乎听不见，洞口是雪。

branches.en: THE STATE ITSELF: the body's heat, pulse and fuel use all fall to a floor that still supports life.
branches.cn: 状态本身：体温、脉搏与燃料消耗都降到仍能维持生命的下限。

branches.en: TIME AND GROUP: the noun also measures how long the wait lasts and marks how a given animal performs it.
branches.cn: 时间与类群：这个名词还计量等待多久，并标出某类动物的具体做法。

branches.en: BORROWED WAIT: a machine or an industry copies the shape, stopping activity while preserving what matters.
branches.cn: 借来的等待：机器或行业复制这个外形，停掉活动却保住要紧之物。

branches.en: ENGINEERED TORPOR: spaceflight proposes to impose the state deliberately to save mass.
branches.cn: 设计出来的昏睡：航天设想人为施加此状态以节省载荷。

branches.en: MEDICAL COOLING: hospitals induce a mild version to slow tissue demand.
branches.cn: 医疗降温：医院诱导轻度版本以降低组织需求。

intro.en: Hibernation is a Latin verb plus a noun suffix, and nearly every part of the family can be read off the same winter root.
intro.cn: hibernation 是一个拉丁动词加名词后缀，词族中几乎每个成员都能沿同一个「冬天」词根读出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin hiems 'winter' gives hibernus 'wintry', which gives hibernare 'to winter'; -atio supplies the action noun, -or the agent and -aculum the place.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 hiems「冬天」生出 hibernus「冬季的」，再生动词 hibernare「过冬」；-atio 提供动作名词，-or 表施动者，-aculum 表场所。

items.example: Pre-hibernation feeding doubled the animal's weight.
