definition_zh: 等级制度；层级体系；统治集团；阶层
definition_en: a system in which people or things are arranged in ranks, with each level ranking above or below another
core_image: 一座一级一级向上收窄的金字塔，每层只对紧挨着的上一层负责
scene: 这里指「等级制度」。 In the hospital, a strict hierarchy decides who may overrule whom during an emergency.
sceneCN: 这里 hierarchy 是「等级体系」（第 1 个义项：组织内部按上下级排列的层级结构）；句意：在医院里，一套严格的等级体系决定紧急情况下谁可以否决谁。场景要点：手术台旁不同颜色的工牌、由下向上的汇报链、每一层只对紧挨着的上一层负责。

pos.zh: 等级制度；层级体系；阶层
（生物学）分类层级；（计算机）层次结构

derivatives.zh: 等级制的；按等级划分的
等级体系中的高层人物；高级教士
等级体系的（较少用变体）

senses.title: A ranked organisation of people
senses.definition: a system in which people or positions are arranged in ranks, so that each rank has authority over the one below it
senses.definitionCN: 把人或职位按等级排列的体系，每一级对下一级拥有权威
senses.example: The firm's hierarchy puts every decision through three levels of approval.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的等级体系让每项决定都要经过三层审批。
senses.why: The core image is a pyramid that narrows as it rises: each level holds authority over the level beneath it, and the shape of the whole depends on that step-by-step arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一座向上收窄的金字塔：每一级对下面一级拥有权威，整体的形状就取决于这种逐级排列。

senses.title: A ranking by importance
senses.definition: an ordering of things from most to least important, powerful, or urgent
senses.definitionCN: 按重要、强大或紧急程度从高到低排列的顺序
senses.example: The report sets out a hierarchy of risks, from flooding to noise.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出了一个风险层级，从洪水一直到噪音。
senses.why: The pyramid can also be built from things rather than people: what sits near the top matters more, and what sits below can wait. The vertical order becomes a scale of value.
senses.whyCN: 这座金字塔也可以由事物而不是人来搭建：靠近顶端的更重要，下面的可以等。垂直顺序由此变成价值尺度。

senses.title: The ruling group at the top
senses.definition: the small group of people who hold the highest positions and control an organisation or society
senses.definitionCN: 占据最高位置、控制某一组织或社会的一小群人
senses.example: Reform was blocked by the party hierarchy.
senses.exampleCN: 改革被党的上层集团阻挠了。
senses.why: By a common shift, the name of the structure comes to mean the people at its narrow top. The pyramid is reduced to its peak, and 'the hierarchy' becomes 'those who decide'.
senses.whyCN: 一种常见的转喻：结构的名称变成了结构顶端那一小群人。金字塔被缩减为塔尖，the hierarchy 也就成了“决定者”。

senses.title: Biological classification ranks
senses.definition: the nested series of categories used to classify organisms, from kingdom down to species
senses.definitionCN: 用于对生物分类的一整套嵌套范畴，从界一直到种
senses.example: Linnaeus arranged living things in a hierarchy of kingdom, class, order, genus and species.
senses.exampleCN: 林奈把生物安排进界、纲、目、属、种这样的层级中。
senses.why: Taxonomy is a pyramid of sets: each rank contains the ranks below it, so a species sits inside a genus, a genus inside a family. The word's vertical shape fits nested classification exactly.
senses.whyCN: 分类学是一个集合的金字塔：每一级都包含下面几级，所以种在属内，属在科内。这个词的垂直形状恰好适合嵌套分类。

senses.title: A layered structure in computing
senses.definition: an arrangement of files, data, or system layers in which each level is contained in or depends on the level above
senses.definitionCN: 文件、数据或系统层次的安排方式，每一层被上一层包含或依赖上一层
senses.example: The folder hierarchy puts every image under its project year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个文件夹层级把每张图片放在对应的项目年份之下。
senses.why: A file tree is a pyramid drawn sideways: one root, branching levels, each item belonging to exactly one parent. The social image survives as containment and dependence rather than authority.
senses.whyCN: 文件树是把金字塔横着画：一个根、逐层分支、每一项只属于一个父项。社会意象在这里保存为包含与依赖，而不是权威。

senses.title: The nine orders of angels
senses.titleCN: 天使九阶：最初的神学义
senses.definition: in Christian theology, the ranked divisions of angels described by Dionysius the Areopagite; the word's earliest English sense
senses.definitionCN: 基督教神学中由伪丢尼修描述的天使等级划分；这是该词最早的英语义项
senses.example: Medieval writers mapped the nine angelic hierarchy onto the nine spheres of heaven.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪作家把天使九阶对应到九重天球上。
senses.why: The word entered English in the late 14th century as a name for the sacred order of angels. Its first hierarchy was not a company but a cosmos: ranks of being, each closer to the divine than the one below.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在 14 世纪晚期进入英语时，是天使神圣秩序的名称。它最初的层级不是公司，而是宇宙：存在的等级，每一级都比下一级更接近神。

senses.title: The order of the clergy
senses.definition: the ranked order of clergy, from deacon and priest up to bishop and pope
senses.definitionCN: 神职人员的等级秩序，从执事、司铎一直向上到主教与教宗
senses.example: A bishop's place in the hierarchy was fixed by canon law.
senses.exampleCN: 主教在教阶体系中的位置由教会法规定。
senses.why: The Greek source means 'rule of a high priest', so the church is where the word feels most at home. Each rank holds sacred office over the rank below, and the ladder runs up to a single summit.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源头意为“大祭司的统治”，因此教会是这个词最如鱼得水的地方。每一级对下一级拥有圣职权威，阶梯一直通向唯一的顶端。

senses.title: A hierarchy of knowledge or values
senses.definition: an abstract ordering in which ideas, laws, or values are ranked as more fundamental than others
senses.definitionCN: 把观念、法律或价值按根本程度排列的抽象秩序
senses.example: In legal theory, the constitution sits at the top of a hierarchy of norms.
senses.exampleCN: 在法律理论中，宪法位于规范层级的顶端。
senses.why: Once the image is abstract, anything that can be 'higher' or 'lower' in rank can form a hierarchy: norms, needs, genres, values. The pyramid becomes a way of saying that some things rest on others.
senses.whyCN: 一旦意象抽象化，任何能在等级上分“高下”的东西都能构成 hierarchy：规范、需求、文类、价值。金字塔变成一种说法，表示某些事物依托于另一些事物。

intro.en: Hierarchy began as a word for the ranks of angels, built from Greek words for 'sacred' and 'rule'. Its modern organisational sense is much later. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hierarchy 最初是天使等级的名称，由希腊语“神圣”与“统治”两个词构成。它现代的组织义要晚得多。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as jerarchie / ierarchie, meaning 'rank in the sacred order' and 'one of the three divisions of the nine orders of angels'; loosely also 'rule, dominion'.
items.cn: 最早以 jerarchie／ierarchie 记录于 14 世纪晚期，意为“神圣秩序中的等级”以及“天使九阶中三大划分之一”；宽泛地也指“统治、管辖”。

items.en: From Old French ierarchie (14c., Modern French hiérarchie), from Medieval Latin hierarchia 'ranked division of angels', the system of Dionysius the Areopagite.
items.cn: 来自古法语 ierarchie（14 世纪，现代法语 hiérarchie），再来自中世纪拉丁语 hierarchia“天使的等级划分”，即伪丢尼修的体系。

items.en: Greek hierarkhia meant 'rule of a high priest', from hierarkhēs 'high priest, leader of sacred rites': ta hiera 'the sacred rites' (from hieros 'sacred') plus arkhein 'to lead, rule'.
items.cn: 希腊语 hierarkhia 意为“大祭司的统治”，来自 hierarkhēs“大祭司、圣礼的主持者”：ta hiera“圣礼”（出自 hieros“神圣”）加 arkhein“引领、统治”。

items.en: The sense 'ranked organisation of persons or things' is recorded in English by the 1610s, at first of the clergy. It was probably reinforced by the unrelated English word higher, which sounds like the start of hierarchy.
items.cn: “人或事物的等级组织”这一义项在 17 世纪 10 年代有记录，最初用于神职人员。它很可能被无关的英语词 higher 强化，因为 higher 听起来像 hierarchy 的开头。

items.en: The word extends to secular institutions, then to natural classification. Taxonomy, army ranks and civil service grades all become hierarchies in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到世俗机构，再扩展到自然分类。分类学、军衔与文官等级在日常语言中都成了 hierarchy。

items.en: Management theory, linguistics and computing adopt it: chain of command, syntactic hierarchy, folder hierarchy. The Greek sacred order becomes a general model of layered structure.
items.cn: 管理学、语言学与计算机科学采用它：指挥链、句法层级、文件夹层级。希腊的神圣秩序变成了分层结构的一般模型。

note.en: The first group separates the noun from its adjective and person forms, and warns about the unrelated word higher; the second group compares ways of ordering people and things.
note.cn: 第一组把名词与它的形容词、指人形式分开，并提醒注意无关的 higher；第二组比较排列人与事物的不同说法。

entries.definition: arranged in ranks, or organised by levels of authority. It describes the shape; hierarchy is the shape itself.
entries.definitionCN: 按等级排列的，或按权威层级组织的。它描述形状；hierarchy 是形状本身。

entries.definition: a person at the top of a hierarchy, especially a senior cleric. It names one holder of rank, not the system of ranks.
entries.definitionCN: 等级体系顶端的人，尤指高级教士。它命名一位占据等级的人，而不是等级体系。

entries.definition: an uncommon variant of hierarchical. It is best avoided when hierarchical is available, since the two are easily confused in writing.
entries.definitionCN: hierarchical 的不常见变体。既然有 hierarchical，最好避免使用，因为两者在书面上极易混淆。

entries.definition: the comparative of high. It is not related to hierarchy, though its sound probably helped the modern sense of ranked organisation take hold.
entries.definitionCN: high 的比较级。它与 hierarchy 没有词源关系，但它的读音很可能帮助了现代“等级组织”义项扎根。

entries.definition: a single level or position in an order. Rank is one rung; hierarchy is the whole ladder and the rule that connects its rungs.
entries.definitionCN: 秩序中的单个级别或位置。rank 是一级横档；hierarchy 是整架梯子以及连接各横档的规则。

entries.definition: the way things are arranged, or a sequence. Order can be flat and neutral, like alphabetical order; hierarchy always implies higher and lower.
entries.definitionCN: 事物被安排的方式，或序列。order 可以是平铺中性的，如字母顺序；hierarchy 总含高下之分。

entries.definition: the informal ranking of status within a group, originally observed in hens. It is vivid and colloquial; hierarchy is neutral and structural.
entries.definitionCN: 群体内部非正式的位次排序，最初来自对鸡群的观察。它形象而口语化；hierarchy 中性且结构化。

entries.definition: the line through which orders pass from superior to subordinate. It stresses communication and obedience, while hierarchy stresses the whole ranked structure.
entries.definitionCN: 命令由上级传到下级的线路。它强调传达与服从，hierarchy 则强调整个等级结构。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Greek hieros 'sacred' plus arkhein 'to rule', and the arch- family that still marks rule in English.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：希腊语 hieros“神圣”加 arkhein“统治”，以及英语中仍标记“统治”的 arch- 词族。

normal.en: Hierarchy literally joins 'sacred' and 'rule': its first home was the order of angels, not the office org chart.
normal.cn: hierarchy 字面上把“神圣”与“统治”连在一起：它最初的家是天使的秩序，而不是办公室的组织图。

normal.en: The arch- in hierarchy is the same arch- that rules in monarchy, anarchy and patriarch: arkhein means 'to lead, rule'.
normal.cn: hierarchy 里的 arch- 与 monarchy、anarchy、patriarch 中表示统治的 arch- 相同：arkhein 意为“引领、统治”。

normal.en: Hierarchy and higher are not related. The resemblance is a coincidence that probably helped the modern meaning feel natural.
normal.cn: hierarchy 与 higher 没有词源关系。这种相似是巧合，但它很可能让现代词义显得更自然。

normal.en: A hierarchy of needs is a real fixed phrase from psychology: needs are stacked, with basic ones below and refined ones above.
normal.cn: hierarchy of needs 是心理学中真实的固定说法：需求被堆叠起来，基本需求在下，精致需求在上。

normal.en: In computing, a folder hierarchy is a tree: one root, many branches, every item with exactly one parent.
normal.cn: 在计算机中，文件夹层级是一棵树：一个根、许多分支，每一项只有一个父项。

abstract.en: Picture a pyramid of stone steps: the base is wide, the top is narrow, and each step exists only because the one below holds it up.
abstract.cn: 想象一座石阶金字塔：底部宽，顶端窄，每一级之所以存在，是因为下面一级托着它。

abstract.en: The same pyramid can be made of people, ranks, species, files or values. What stays constant is that some things rest on others and none may float.
abstract.cn: 同一座金字塔可以由人、军衔、物种、文件或价值搭成。不变的是：某些事物依托于另一些事物，没有谁能悬空。

abstract.en: When people say 'the hierarchy', they mean the narrow top of the pyramid: the structure has shrunk to the few who decide.
abstract.cn: 当人们说 the hierarchy，指的是金字塔狭窄的顶端：整个结构被缩减为少数做决定的人。

examples.en: The old monastery kept a hierarchy so precise that even the order of seating was recorded.
examples.cn: 那座古老修道院的等级秩序精确到连座次都被记录下来。

examples.en: Flat teams often claim to have no hierarchy, yet informal rankings reappear within weeks.
examples.cn: 扁平化团队常声称没有等级，但非正式的位次几周内就会重新出现。

examples.en: The database stores every page in a hierarchy of folders rather than a single list.
examples.cn: 这个数据库把每个页面存放在文件夹层级中，而不是一张单层列表里。

dict_mnemonic.text: “海尔拉基”——海尔把员工拉成一级一级的基座，越往上人越少 → hierarchy 等级制度

root: 源自希腊语 hierarkhia“大祭司的统治”，由 hieros“神圣”+ arkhein“统治”构成，核心是“按等级层层向上、每层对下层拥有权威”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of hierarchy, all grown from one shape: a pyramid of ranks in which each level rests on the one below and answers to the one above.
sensesIntro.cn: hierarchy 的八个义项都从同一个形状长出来：一座等级金字塔，每一级依托下一级，并向上一级负责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrowing pyramid of ranks, each level resting on the one below and answering to the one above.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座逐级收窄的等级金字塔，每层依托下层，并对上层负责。

branches.en: ORGANISATION AND POWER: a ranked body of people, and then the narrow group at its top who actually decide.
branches.cn: 组织与权力：先是按等级排列的人群，再是位于塔尖、真正做决定的那一小群。

branches.en: ORDERING: the same vertical shape ranks risks, needs, norms and values by importance or fundamentality.
branches.cn: 排序：同一垂直形状按重要性或根本性排列风险、需求、规范与价值。

branches.en: BIOLOGY: nested sets reproduce the pyramid exactly, since each taxonomic rank contains the ranks below it.
branches.cn: 生物学：嵌套集合精确复制了金字塔，因为每个分类层级都包含下面几级。

branches.en: COMPUTING: a tree is the pyramid laid on its side, with containment and dependency instead of obedience.
branches.cn: 计算机：树是横放的金字塔，用包含与依赖替代了服从。

branches.en: THE SACRED SOURCE: angels and clergy are the word's first home, where rank means proximity to the divine.
branches.cn: 神圣源头：天使与神职人员是这个词最初的家，等级意味着与神更近。

intro.en: Hierarchy is a Greek compound borrowed through Latin and French: hieros 'sacred' + arkhein 'to rule'. English adds -al, -ic, -ically and -arch to the same stem.
intro.cn: hierarchy 是经拉丁语和法语借入的希腊语复合词：hieros“神圣”+ arkhein“统治”。英语在同一词干上加 -al、-ic、-ically 与 -arch。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin hierarchia and hierarcha carried the Greek word into church writing. The second element, arkhein, is the source of the productive English combining form -arch, meaning 'ruler'.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 hierarchia 与 hierarcha 把这个希腊词带进教会写作。第二个成分 arkhein 是英语能产后缀 -arch（意为“统治者”）的来源。

items.meaningCN: 等级制的；按层级划分的（-ical 构成形容词）
items.example: The archive uses a hierarchical system of folders.
items.exampleCN: 这个档案库使用层级化的文件夹系统。

items.meaning: of or relating to a hierarchy
items.meaningCN: 等级体系的；层级式的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: The diagram shows the hierarchic links between teams.
items.exampleCN: 这张图显示各团队之间的层级联系。

items.meaning: a chief ruler in sacred matters; a high-ranking member of a hierarchy
items.meaningCN: 高级教士；等级体系中的高层人物
items.example: The hierarch blessed the new chapel.
items.exampleCN: 这位高级教士为新礼拜堂祝圣。

items.meaning: in a ranked or layered way
items.example: The data is organised hierarchically, from region to street.
items.exampleCN: 数据按层级组织，从大区一直到街道。

items.meaningCN: 等级体系的（较少使用的形容词变体）
items.example: Older texts prefer hierarchal to hierarchical.
items.exampleCN: 较早的文本更爱用 hierarchal 而不是 hierarchical。

items.meaningCN: 君主制；一人统治（mono- 单一 + -archy 统治）
items.example: The monarchy survived the revolution in a ceremonial form.
items.exampleCN: 君主制以礼仪形式在革命后存续下来。

items.meaning: a state without government or order
items.meaningCN: 无政府状态；混乱（an- 无 + -archy 统治）
items.example: The power cut left the station in near anarchy.
items.exampleCN: 停电让车站几乎陷入无秩序状态。

items.example: The company drifted into an oligarchy of three directors.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司逐渐变成三位董事的寡头统治。

items.meaning: the male head of a family or church
items.meaningCN: 家长；宗主教（patri- 父 + -arch 统治者）
items.exampleCN: 宗主教带领了游行队伍。

items.meaning: a bishop of the highest rank
a chief magistrate in ancient Athens
items.example: The archon was chosen by lot each year.
items.exampleCN: 执政官每年以抽签方式选出。

latinEntries.structure: Greek hierarkhia, borrowed into Medieval Latin
latinEntries.meaning: the ranked division of angels; sacred rule
latinEntries.meaningCN: 天使的等级划分；神圣统治

latinEntries.meaning: a high priest, one who rules in sacred things

definition_zh: 与古埃及象形文字有关的；用图画符号写成的；难以辨认的；（复数名词）象形文字体系
definition_en: relating to Egyptian picture writing; written in picture signs; difficult to decipher; as a plural noun, the picture script itself
core_image: 石柱上层层叠叠的鸟兽符号排成一列，像一套只有祭司才会读的图画语言
scene: 讲解员把投影打在神庙的浮雕上。The hieroglyphic band along the wall spells out the pharaoh's titles.
sceneCN: 这里 hieroglyphic 指「用象形文字写成的」（第 2 个义项：以图画符号书写）；句意为墙上那条象形文字带拼出了法老的头衔。

pos.zh: 象形文字的；用图画符号写成的；难辨认的
（复数）象形文字体系；单个象形符号

derivatives.zh: hieroglyphic 去掉 -ic（逆构名词）→ 单个象形字符
hieroglyphic + -s（集合名词后缀）→ 象形文字体系
hieroglyphical + -ly（副词后缀）→ 以象形文字方式
hieroglyphic + -al（形容词后缀）→ 象形文字的（旧式变体）
hieroglyph + -ist（从业者后缀）→ 象形文字研究者

senses.title: Relating to Egyptian picture writing
senses.definition: connected with the ancient Egyptian script whose signs are pictures
senses.definitionCN: 与以图画为符号的古埃及文字有关的
senses.example: The hieroglyphic texts on the tomb wall are still being translated.
senses.exampleCN: 墓壁上的象形文字文本仍在翻译中。
senses.why: the adjective was coined from the Greek noun for sacred carving, so it first labels the Egyptian script.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由表示「神圣雕刻」的希腊名词造出，因此最初标定埃及文字。

senses.title: Written in picture signs
senses.definition: composed or printed in a script made of picture signs rather than ordinary letters
senses.definitionCN: 用图画符号而非普通字母组成或印出的
senses.example: The hieroglyphic band along the wall spells out the pharaoh's titles.
senses.exampleCN: 墙上那条象形文字带拼出了法老的头衔。
senses.why: once the adjective describes the medium, it can describe any text written in that medium.
senses.whyCN: 形容词一旦描述书写媒介，就能描述任何用该媒介写成的文本。

senses.title: Difficult to decipher
senses.definition: so obscure or complicated that it is hard to read or understand
senses.definitionCN: 晦涩或复杂到难以阅读和理解
senses.example: The lease was drafted in hieroglyphic prose that no tenant could follow.
senses.exampleCN: 这份租约用晦涩难懂的文句写成，没有租户能看明白。
senses.why: a script that most readers cannot read becomes a metaphor for any obscure style.
senses.whyCN: 大多数人读不懂的文字，会成为任何晦涩文风的隐喻。

senses.title: Decorated with symbolic figures
senses.definition: ornamented with carved or painted symbolic figures rather than with plain patterns
senses.definitionCN: 以雕刻或绘制的象征图形而非素朴图案装饰的
senses.example: The frieze is hieroglyphic rather than purely ornamental.
senses.exampleCN: 这条饰带带象征图形，而不只是纯装饰。
senses.why: the adjective can describe the look of a surface covered with sign-like figures, not only its text.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也能描述布满符号状图形的表面外观，而不只描述文本。

senses.title: The script as a whole (plural noun)
senses.titleCN: 象形文字体系（复数名词）
senses.definition: the picture writing of ancient Egypt considered as one system
senses.definitionCN: 把古埃及图画文字视为一个整体体系
senses.example: Hieroglyphics remained unread until scholars studied the Rosetta Stone.
senses.exampleCN: 在学者研究罗塞塔石碑之前，象形文字一直无人能读。
senses.why: English turns many adjectives into plural nouns with -s; here the plural names a whole body of writing.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用 -s 把形容词转为复数名词；这里的复数指一整套文字。

senses.title: A single picture sign (noun)
senses.definition: one picture sign used in such a script
senses.definitionCN: 这类文字中使用的一个图画符号
senses.example: One hieroglyphic was carved into the lintel above the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门上的过梁刻着一个象形符号。
senses.why: the same adjective is used as a noun for the unit it describes, a common English shift.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词被用作名词来指它所描述的单位，这是英语常见的转类。

senses.title: Having a sacred or priestly tone
senses.definition: carrying the solemn, priestly quality of a temple inscription
senses.definitionCN: 带有神庙铭文那种庄严、祭司式的气质
senses.example: The old chant had a hieroglyphic gravity that silenced the room.
senses.exampleCN: 那首古老的吟唱带着一种象形铭文般的庄严，让全场安静下来。
senses.why: because the root hieros means sacred, the adjective can lend a priestly tone to non-textual things.
senses.whyCN: 由于词根 hieros 意为神圣，这个形容词能给非文本事物添上祭司式的语气。

senses.title: Deliberately cryptic in style
senses.definition: expressed in a coded or deliberately obscure style
senses.definitionCN: 以密码式或刻意晦涩的风格表达
senses.example: The memo was hieroglyphic to everyone outside the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 对委员会以外的人而言，那份备忘录像天书一样。
senses.why: the unreadable-script sense extends to any writing that seems designed to exclude outsiders.
senses.whyCN: 「读不懂的文字」这一义扩展到任何似乎故意排除外人的写法。

intro.en: Hieroglyphic is the adjective built on Greek hieroglyphikos, 'of sacred carving'. English borrowed the adjective before it made the shorter noun hieroglyph.
intro.cn: hieroglyphic 是建立在希腊 hieroglyphikos「神圣雕刻的」之上的形容词。英语先借入形容词，之后才造出更短的名词 hieroglyph。

items.en: Hieros meant 'sacred'; the adjective marks the carvings as temple signs rather than ordinary writing.
items.cn: hieros 意为「神圣」；这个形容词把雕刻标为神庙符号，而非普通文字。

items.en: Glyphein meant 'to carve', naming the tool and the cut behind every sign.
items.cn: glyphein 意为「雕刻」，命名每个符号背后的工具与刻痕。

items.en: The adjective hieroglyphikos described sacred carved signs and the writing made from them.
items.cn: 形容词 hieroglyphikos 描述神圣雕刻符号以及由它们构成的文字。

items.en: Late Latin kept the Greek adjective as hieroglyphicus, the form learned English borrowed.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语把希腊形容词保留为 hieroglyphicus，学术英语借用的正是这个形式。

items.en: English used hieroglyphic for Egyptian writing, and later for any picture-like or unreadable mark.
items.cn: 英语用 hieroglyphic 指埃及文字，后来也指任何图画式或难读的记号。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the adjective appears in English dictionaries with slightly different first dates, though its Greek and Latin chain is clear.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：各词典给出的英语首见年代略有差异，但其希腊与拉丁链条清楚。

note.en: Group one holds the noun and the rival scripts most often confused with it; group two holds adjectives for writing that is hard to read.
note.cn: 第一组是最常与该词混淆的名词与竞争性文字体系；第二组是形容文字难读的形容词。

entries.definition: The countable noun for a single sign; hieroglyphic is the adjective or the plural name of the system.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个字符的可数名词；hieroglyphic 是形容词或指整个体系的复数名词。

entries.definition: Any single character shape in a font or symbol set; it lacks the sacred Egyptian reference.
entries.definitionCN: 字体或符号集中的任何单个字形；不含埃及神圣语境。

entries.definition: The wedge-based script of Mesopotamia; it is a rival system, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 美索不达米亚的楔形文字；是另一套体系，并非同义词。

entries.definition: Describing any script that uses pictures; hieroglyphic is the specific Egyptian and sacred case.
entries.definitionCN: 描述任何使用图画的文字；hieroglyphic 是埃及的、带神圣色彩的具体一类。

entries.definition: Written or said in a way that hides the meaning; it stresses intention, not the script.
entries.definitionCN: 以隐藏含义的方式写出或说出；强调意图，而非文字体系。

entries.definition: So badly formed that the letters cannot be read at all; hieroglyphic can still be decipherable.
entries.definitionCN: 字形太差以致完全读不出；hieroglyphic 仍可能是可解读的。

entries.definition: Using signs to represent ideas; it is broader and lacks the carving image.
entries.definitionCN: 用符号代表概念；范围更广，且没有雕刻意象。

entries.definition: Acting as a representative mark of a group or idea; it stresses belonging rather than writing.
entries.definitionCN: 作为群体或观念的代表性标记；强调归属，而非书写。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Greek roots, the real adjective chain and the real plural noun.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实希腊词根、真实的形容词链条与真实的复数名词。

normal.en: hieros 'sacred' plus glyphein 'carve' gives the adjective its two halves.
normal.cn: hieros「神圣」加 glyphein「雕刻」构成这个形容词的两半。

normal.en: The adjective entered English before the shorter noun hieroglyph.
normal.cn: 形容词比更短的名词 hieroglyph 更早进入英语。

normal.en: Hieroglyphics with -s names the whole script, not several separate signs.
normal.cn: 带 -s 的 hieroglyphics 指整套文字，而非几个分离的符号。

normal.en: The Rosetta Stone is the real key that made hieroglyphics readable.
normal.cn: 罗塞塔石碑是让象形文字变得可读的真实钥匙。

normal.en: In ordinary speech hieroglyphic often means simply unreadable.
normal.cn: 在日常口语中，hieroglyphic 常常只表示「读不懂」。

abstract.en: A hieroglyphic wall is a sentence that refuses to be spoken.
abstract.cn: 象形文字的墙面，是一句拒绝被说出口的话。

abstract.en: It is writing that looks back at the reader.
abstract.cn: 它是会回望读者的文字。

abstract.en: Deciphering it feels like lifting a lid off a very old box.
abstract.cn: 解读它，像揭开一只很旧的箱子的盖子。

examples.en: The hieroglyphic inscription records a treaty between two cities.
examples.cn: 这段象形文字铭文记录了两座城市之间的条约。

examples.en: Her handwriting is almost hieroglyphic.
examples.cn: 她的笔迹几乎像象形文字一样难认。

examples.en: Hieroglyphics were used in Egypt for thousands of years.
examples.cn: 象形文字在埃及使用了数千年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「hiero（神圣）+ glyph（刻）+ ic」——刻在神庙上的神圣图形 → 象形文字的

root: 希腊 hieros「神圣」+ glyphein「雕刻」→ hieroglyphikos；经晚期拉丁 hieroglyphicus 进入英语作 hieroglyphic，先为形容词，后衍生名词 hieroglyph。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the Egyptian adjective to the written medium, then to the unreadable style and the plural name of the whole script.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「埃及的形容词」走到书写媒介，再走到难读的文风与整套文字的复数名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carved band of birds and eyes running along a temple wall, readable only to those who hold the key.
core.cn: 核心意象：神庙墙上一条由鸟与眼睛组成的雕刻带，只有掌握钥匙的人才能读。

branches.en: SACRED LOOK: the Egyptian reference and the symbolic frieze both describe a carved, sign-covered surface.
branches.cn: 神圣外观：埃及指向与象征饰带都在描述布满符号的雕刻表面。

branches.en: MEDIUM AND UNIT: writing in picture signs and one such sign are the same medium seen whole and seen singly.
branches.cn: 媒介与单位：用图画符号书写与单个这样的符号，是同一媒介的整体与单点。

branches.en: UNREADABLE STYLE: an obscure text and a deliberately coded memo both shut the reader out.
branches.cn: 难读的文风：晦涩文本与刻意加密的备忘录都把读者挡在外面。

branches.en: WHOLE SYSTEM: the plural noun gathers every sign into one named script.
branches.cn: 整套体系：复数名词把所有符号收进一个有名字的文字体系。

branches.en: PRIESTLY GRAVITY: the sacred root lends its tone even to a chant.
branches.cn: 祭司式的庄严：神圣词根把语气借给了吟唱。

intro.en: Hieroglyphic is a Greek adjective with a Latin carrier form, and its parts also build the shorter noun and several technical words.
intro.cn: hieroglyphic 是一个带拉丁中转形式的希腊形容词，它的各部分还构成更短的名词与若干技术词。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin hieroglyphicus carried the Greek adjective, and the neuter plural hieroglyphica named sacred carved signs.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁 hieroglyphicus 承载希腊形容词，中性复数 hieroglyphica 指神圣雕刻符号。

items.example: The root marks the writing as temple property.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把文字标为神庙之物。

items.example: The root names the cut that makes each sign.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名刻出每个符号的动作。

items.example: The suffix turns the compound into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把复合词变成描述词。

items.example: A hieroglyph stood above the gate.
items.exampleCN: 门上刻着一个象形字符。

items.meaningCN: 神圣雕刻的；象形文字的

items.exampleCN: 象形文字保存在神庙墙上。

items.example: The sign uses a rare glyph.
items.exampleCN: 这个标牌用了罕见字形。

items.example: Hieratic was the quick hand of the temple scribes.
items.exampleCN: 僧侣体是神庙书吏的快写体。

latinEntries.structure: hieroglyphica (Late Latin neuter plural, from Greek)

hieroglyphic + -s（集合名词后缀）→ 整套象形文字
hieroglyphic + -al（形容词后缀）→ 象形文字的（旧式）
hieroglyphical + -ly（副词后缀）→ 以象形文字方式
hieroglyph + -ist（从业者后缀）→ 象形文字研究者

definition_zh: 高地；高地区域；高地地带；山地牧场
definition_en: land that is higher than the country around it, especially a cool, hilly region used for grazing
core_image: 地面整体被抬高，形成一片起伏的草坡，风从坡顶掠过
scene: 云层贴着草坡移动，风比谷底冷得多。Sheep graze on the highland above the village.
sceneCN: 此处指「高于周围、气候较冷的高处土地」（第 1 个义项：整体抬升的起伏地带）；句意为羊群在村子上方的高地上吃草。图中可辨识物件：贴坡移动的云、起伏草坡、羊群、谷底与高处的温差。

pos.zh: 高地；高地区域；（复数）高地地带
高地的（如 highland cattle、highland village）

senses.title: Land higher than its surroundings
senses.definition: ground that stands above the lower country around it
senses.definitionCN: 高出周围低地的地面
senses.example: Sheep graze on the highland above the village.
senses.exampleCN: 羊群在村子上方的高地上吃草。
senses.why: The compound is literal: high land. The defining feature is relative height, not rock or climate.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词是字面的：高的土地。定义特征是相对高度，而不是岩石或气候。

senses.title: A highland region in the plural
senses.definition: the highlands, used for a whole tract of elevated country
senses.definitionCN: 用复数指一整片抬高的地区
senses.example: Rain falls more heavily in the highlands.
senses.exampleCN: 高地区域的降雨更多。
senses.why: The plural turns elevated ground into a named region, the counterpart of the lowlands.
senses.whyCN: 复数把抬高的地面变成一个有名字的地区，与「低地」一词相对。

senses.title: The Scottish Highlands
senses.definition: the mountainous northern and western part of Scotland, with a distinct culture and history
senses.definitionCN: 苏格兰北部与西部的山地地区，有独特的文化与历史
senses.example: The Highlands are famous for deep valleys and bare ridges.
senses.exampleCN: 苏格兰高地以深谷与裸露山脊闻名。
senses.why: A capitalised proper name fixes the general word to one famous region.
senses.whyCN: 带大写的专名把这个一般词固定到一个著名的地区。

senses.title: A high-altitude ecological zone
senses.definition: the belt of land above the surrounding lowland, with cooler climate and different vegetation
senses.definitionCN: 位于周围低地之上、气候更冷、植被不同的地带
senses.example: Highland plants grow low to escape the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 高地植物贴地生长以躲避风。
senses.why: Ecology turns relative height into a measurable zone with its own species and climate.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把相对高度变成一个有自身物种与气候的可测量地带。

senses.title: Attributive: of the high country
senses.definition: used before a noun for the highland version of a thing, breed or place
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，表示某物、某品种或某地的高地类型
senses.example: Highland cattle have long hair and broad horns.
senses.exampleCN: 高地牛有长毛和宽角。
senses.why: The noun marks the altitude band where the following thing belongs.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词标出后面事物所属的海拔带。

senses.title: Hill pasture used for grazing
senses.definition: rough elevated grassland used for sheep or cattle in summer
senses.definitionCN: 夏季用来放羊或放牛的粗放高地草场
senses.example: The highland is open to grazing from May to October.
senses.exampleCN: 这片高地牧场从五月到十月开放放牧。
senses.why: People use the word for the land's economic role, not only its height.
senses.whyCN: 人们用这个词指土地的经济角色，而不只是它的高度。

senses.title: Highland people and culture
senses.definition: the communities and traditions of a highland region, contrasted with lowland society
senses.definitionCN: 高地地区的社群与传统，与低地社会相对
senses.example: Highland music travelled far beyond the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 高地音乐传到了群山之外很远的地方。
senses.why: A shared landscape produces shared customs, so the land word becomes a cultural label.
senses.whyCN: 共同的地貌产生共同的习俗，于是土地词变成文化标签。

senses.title: The highland side of a contrast
senses.definition: the elevated half of a regional highland-lowland division, used as a general concept
senses.definitionCN: 地区性高低二分中抬高的那一半，用作一般概念
senses.example: The highland and lowland economies depend on each other.
senses.exampleCN: 高地与低地经济彼此依赖。
senses.why: Once a region is divided by height, each half becomes a category that planners and historians can name.
senses.whyCN: 一片地区一旦按高度划分，每一半都成为规划者与历史学家可以命名的类别。

intro.en: Highland is a native English compound of high, from Old English hēah, and land. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: highland 是英语本族复合词，由来自古英语 hēah 的 high 与 land 组合而成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old English hēah meant 'high, tall, exalted'; it is the native adjective behind modern high.
items.cn: 古英语 hēah 意为「高的、高大的、尊贵的」；它是现代 high 背后的本族形容词。

items.en: Old English land meant 'land, country, territory', a native Germanic word shared across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 古英语 land 意为「土地、国家、领地」，是日耳曼语族共有的本土词。

items.en: Middle English high and land were both common; the compound highland appears later, when regional height contrasts needed a fixed term.
items.cn: 中古英语 high 与 land 都已常用；复合词 highland 出现较晚，是在地区高度对比需要固定说法之时。

items.en: The capitalised Highlands became the standard name for the Scottish uplands, especially after the eighteenth-century romantic interest in mountain scenery.
items.cn: 带大写的 Highlands 成为苏格兰高地的标准名称，尤其在 18 世纪对山地风景的浪漫兴趣兴起之后。

items.en: Modern geography uses highland as an altitude and relief class, often paired with lowland in regional descriptions.
items.cn: 现代地理学把 highland 用作海拔与起伏等级，常与 lowland 配对使用于区域描述。

items.en: Both elements are secure and native; only the first date of the compound is approximate. Neither element has a Latin etymon.
items.cn: 两个成分都可靠且为本族词，只有复合词的首见年代为约数。两个成分都没有拉丁词源。

note.en: The first group holds words built on high or land; the second holds words for elevated country.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在 high 或 land 上的词；第二组是表示抬高地区的词。

entries.definition: Land lower than its surroundings; the direct height opposite, built the same way.
entries.definitionCN: 低于周围的地面；在高度上正相反，构词方式相同。

entries.definition: A person from a highland region; it adds -er to the same compound.
entries.definitionCN: 来自高地地区的人；是在同一复合词上加 -er。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'tall or elevated'; alone it describes height, not a region.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「高的、抬高的」形容词；单独使用时描述高度，而不是地区。

entries.definition: The plural of highland; it can also be a proper name for a specific region.
entries.definitionCN: highland 的复数；也可作为某一具体地区的专名。

entries.definition: Land higher than the nearby valleys; it is more neutral and less tied to a named region than highland.
entries.definitionCN: 高于附近谷地的土地；比 highland 更中性，也更少绑定某一具名地区。

entries.definition: A high area with a flat top; highland may be rolling, but a plateau specifically insists on flatness.
entries.definitionCN: 顶部平坦的高地；highland 可以是起伏的，而高原特别强调平坦。

entries.definition: Open rough upland, often peaty and wet; it adds vegetation and soil to the height.
entries.definitionCN: 开阔粗放的高地，常含泥炭且潮湿；它在高度之外加了植被与土壤。

entries.definition: A broad flat elevated region; it describes the shape directly, while highland describes relative position.
entries.definitionCN: 宽阔平坦的高地；直接描述形状，而 highland 描述相对位置。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two native elements, the real proper name and the altitude contrast with lowland.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个本族成分、真实的专名，以及与 lowland 的海拔对比。

normal.en: high + land: literally 'high land'.
normal.cn: high + land：字面就是「高的土地」。

normal.en: The family runs highland, highlands, highlander, highland cattle, highland fling.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 highland、highlands、highlander、highland cattle、highland fling。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: highland area, highland region, highland village, highland climate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 highland area、highland region、highland village、highland climate。

normal.en: Lowland is the mirror compound: same structure, opposite height.
normal.cn: lowland 是镜像复合词：结构相同，高度相反。

normal.en: The Highlands capitalises the word for Scotland's uplands.
normal.cn: The Highlands 用大写把这个词固定为苏格兰高地。

abstract.en: Picture a green blanket lifted at one end so that it slopes upward.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绿色毯子一端被提起，于是向上倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture clouds dragging along a slope instead of floating above it.
abstract.cn: 想象云层沿着坡面拖行，而不是飘在上方。

abstract.en: Picture two maps of the same country, one shaded brown at the top and one green at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个国家的两张地图，一张顶部染褐，一张底部染绿。

examples.en: The highland receives more rain than the coast.
examples.cn: 高地比海岸得到更多降雨。

examples.en: Highland roads close when snow blocks the passes.
examples.cn: 大雪封住山口时，高地公路会封闭。

examples.en: Many Highlanders left for the cities in the nineteenth century.
examples.cn: 19 世纪，许多高地居民迁往城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嗨（hai）+ 兰（lan）+ 的（d）」—— 嗨到高处的草地，风大又冷 → 高地

root: high（古英语 hēah「高的」）+ land（古英语 land「土地」）→ 字面「高的土地」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin with ground above its surroundings, then extend to a region, a famous proper name, an ecological belt, a habitat label, pasture, a culture and one half of a regional contrast.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「高于周围的地面」出发，再扩展到一片地区、一个著名专名、一条生态带、一类生境、牧场、一种文化，以及地区对比中的一半。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rolling surface lifted above the valleys, colder and windier than the ground below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片被抬到谷地之上的起伏地面，比下方更冷、风更大。

branches.en: THE GROUND: a raised stretch, and the plural that makes it a region.
branches.cn: 土地：一段抬高的地面，以及把它变成地区的复数。

branches.en: THE NAME: the Highlands fixes the word to Scotland's uplands.
branches.cn: 名称：The Highlands 把这个词固定为苏格兰高地。

branches.en: THE BELT: altitude creates a zone with its own plants, breeds and weather.
branches.cn: 地带：海拔造出一个拥有自身植物、品种与天气的区域。

branches.en: THE PASTURE: the land's use as summer grazing.
branches.cn: 牧场：这片土地作为夏季放牧之用的角色。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE AND THE DIVISION: shared height makes shared culture and a regional half.
branches.cn: 人与划分：共同的高度造就共同的文化，也构成地区的一半。

intro.en: Highland is a transparent native compound; its family comes from the two elements and from names of highland breeds, dances and places.
intro.cn: highland 是透明的本族复合词；词族来自两个成分，以及高地品种、舞蹈与地名。

latinIntro.en: Neither element has a Latin etymon: high is native Old English hēah and land is Old English land, so the Latin entry list is empty by design.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都没有拉丁词源：high 是古英语本族词 hēah，land 是古英语 land，因此拉丁条目按规则留空。

items.example: The wall is two metres high.
The land rises toward the north.
The highland is cool even in summer.
The highlands feed the main rivers.
items.exampleCN: 高地区域为主要的河流供水。
一位高地居民给队伍带路。

items.meaning: a hardy breed with long hair

items.meaningCN: 一种活泼的苏格兰独舞
items.example: The highland fling ends the evening.
items.exampleCN: 高地弗林舞为夜晚收尾。

items.meaning: the cooler, wetter climate of high ground

items.example: The road drops from highland to lowland.
items.exampleCN: 公路从高地下降到低地。

definition_zh: 最精彩的部分；高亮；强调
definition_en: the best or most important part of something, or a bright area in a picture
core_image: 舞台灯光落在全场最亮的那一小块
scene: 演出的最精彩部分是一段双人舞。The highlight of the show was a duet.
sceneCN: 这里 highlight 是「最精彩的部分」（第 1 个义项）；句意：演出的最精彩部分是一段双人舞。

senses.title: Best part
senses.definition: the best or most exciting part of an event
senses.definitionCN: 事件中最精彩或最激动人心的部分
senses.example: The highlight of the show was a duet.
senses.exampleCN: 演出的最精彩部分是一段双人舞。
senses.why: This is the most common everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常用的日常义项。

senses.title: Bright area
senses.definition: the brightest part of a picture or scene
senses.definitionCN: 画面或场景中最亮的部分
senses.example: Keep the highlights in the photo soft.
senses.exampleCN: 让照片中的高光部分保持柔和。
senses.why: The word keeps its literal sense of bright light.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了「明亮的光」这一本义。

senses.title: Emphasize
senses.definition: to draw attention to something
senses.definitionCN: 引起人们对某事物的注意
senses.example: The report highlights the need for change.
senses.exampleCN: 报告强调了变革的必要性。
senses.why: As a verb it means to make something stand out.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时表示让某事物突显出来。

intro.en: Highlight joins the words high and light.
intro.cn: highlight 由 high 和 light 两个词组合而成。

items.en: Heah meant high or tall.
items.cn: heah 意为高的或高大的。

items.en: Leoht meant light.
items.cn: leoht 意为光。

items.en: High and light often appeared together.
items.cn: high 和 light 经常一起出现。

items.en: Highlight first named the brightest part of a painting.
items.cn: highlight 最初指画中最亮的部分。

items.en: Highlight then came to mean the best part.
items.cn: 后来 highlight 指最精彩的部分。

items.en: As a verb it now means to emphasize.
items.cn: 作动词时，它现在表示强调。

note.en: Highlight is compared with look-alike compounds and with words for the best moment.
note.cn: 把 highlight 与形近复合词以及表示最佳时刻的词作比较。

entries.definition: a pen with bright ink
entries.definitionCN: 荧光笔

entries.definition: an area of high land
entries.definitionCN: 高地

entries.definition: marked or stressed
entries.definitionCN: 被突出的

entries.definition: the highest point
entries.definitionCN: 顶点

entries.definition: the most exciting moment
entries.definitionCN: 高潮

entries.definition: to give special importance to
entries.definitionCN: 强调

normalIntro.en: A highlight is the high light that falls on the best moment.
normalIntro.cn: highlight 就是打在最佳时刻上的那束高光。

normal.en: The highlight of the show was a duet.
normal.cn: 演出的最精彩部分是一段双人舞。

normal.en: Keep the highlights in the photo soft.
normal.cn: 让照片中的高光部分保持柔和。

normal.en: The report highlights the need for change.
normal.cn: 报告强调了变革的必要性。

normal.en: Winning the cup was the highlight of the season.
normal.cn: 捧起奖杯是那个赛季最精彩的时刻。

normal.en: She used a highlighter on the key sentence.
normal.cn: 她用荧光笔标出了关键句。

abstract.en: A highlight is only bright against the rest of the story.
abstract.cn: 亮点之所以亮，是因为故事其余部分作背景。

abstract.en: We remember highlights and call them a life.
abstract.cn: 我们记住高光时刻，然后称它为一生。

abstract.en: To highlight one thing is to hide another.
abstract.cn: 强调一件事，就是让另一件事退到暗处。

examples.en: The highlight of the show was a duet.
examples.cn: 演出的最精彩部分是一段双人舞。

examples.en: The report highlights the need for change.
examples.cn: 报告强调了变革的必要性。

examples.en: Winning the cup was the highlight of the season.
examples.cn: 捧起奖杯是那个赛季最精彩的时刻。

dict_mnemonic.text: highlight 由 high 和 light 合成，字面是「高光」；引申为最精彩的部分，也作动词表示强调、高亮标记。

root: 由 high（高的）与 light（光）合成的现代英语复合词，本指画面中最亮的受光部分，后引申为最精彩的部分与强调。

sensesIntro.en: Highlight can be the best part, the bright area, or the act of emphasizing.
sensesIntro.cn: highlight 可以指最精彩的部分、画面高光，或强调的动作。

core.en: The brightest spot in a scene.

definition_en: to make progress, movement or an effort slower or more difficult
core_image: 一条窄路中间横着一块落石，后面的人只能一点点侧身挪过去
scene: 材料迟迟不到，工人只能在半成品旁边等，工期一天天往后推。Late deliveries hindered progress on the upper floors.
sceneCN: 这里指拖慢工程的推进（第 1 个义项：阻碍进展）；句意为到货太晚妨碍了上层的施工进度。图中可辨识物件：横在路中的落石、侧身通过的人、堆着的半成品。

senses.title: To slow a project
senses.definition: to make a project or task take longer by creating obstacles
senses.definitionCN: 通过制造障碍，让项目或任务花更长时间
senses.example: Missing permits hindered work on the site for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 缺少许可使工地施工拖了好几周。
senses.why: The core sense is being placed behind, and a delay puts a task behind schedule.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是「被放在后面」，而延误就是把任务放到进度后面。

senses.title: To block movement
senses.definition: to make it hard for someone or something to move forward
senses.definitionCN: 使人或物难以前进
senses.example: Fallen trees hindered the rescue teams in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 倒下的树妨碍了山谷里的救援队。
senses.why: This is the physical picture at its simplest: something in the way, a body moving around it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的物理画面：有东西挡路，身体绕着走。

senses.title: To restrain growth
senses.definition: to keep an economy, market or organism from expanding at its potential rate
senses.definitionCN: 使经济、市场或生物体无法按潜在速度扩张
senses.example: Uncertain rules hindered investment in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 规则不明朗抑制了该地区的投资。
senses.why: Growth is a forward motion, and hindering puts weight on it.
senses.whyCN: 增长是向前运动，阻碍就是给它加上重量。

senses.title: To disrupt work or study
senses.definition: to interrupt concentration or routine so that output falls
senses.definitionCN: 打断专注或日常节奏，使产出下降
senses.example: Constant noise hindered her revision for the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 持续的噪声干扰了她的备考复习。
senses.why: Attention is a narrow path, and any obstruction on it costs time.
senses.whyCN: 注意力是一条窄路，路上任何阻碍都要花时间。

senses.title: To obstruct a plan
senses.definition: to act so that a proposal or decision cannot proceed as intended
senses.definitionCN: 采取行动，使提案或决定无法按计划推进
senses.example: Two members hindered the vote by raising procedural objections.
senses.exampleCN: 两名成员提出程序异议，阻挠了表决。
senses.why: Institutions run on procedure, so blocking a step is enough to hold the whole thing back.
senses.whyCN: 机构靠程序运转，卡住一步就足以拖住整件事。

senses.title: To stunt growth or recovery
senses.definition: to prevent a living thing or a recovery from reaching full development
senses.definitionCN: 使生物体或恢复过程无法充分发展
senses.example: Poor light hindered the seedlings after transplanting.
senses.exampleCN: 光照不足抑制了移栽后的幼苗生长。
senses.why: Biology uses the verb for anything that keeps a process below its natural curve.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用这个动词指任何让过程低于其自然曲线的因素。

senses.title: To make a task harder
senses.definition: to raise the effort or cost needed to complete something
senses.definitionCN: 提高完成某事所需的努力或成本
senses.example: The outdated software hindered every update.
senses.exampleCN: 过时的软件让每次更新都更难。
senses.why: Difficulty is friction, and the verb names the extra friction added.
senses.whyCN: 难度就是摩擦，这个词指被加上去的那份额外摩擦。

senses.title: To impair communication
senses.definition: to make exchange of information or cooperation less effective
senses.definitionCN: 使信息交换或合作效果变差
senses.example: Different reporting formats hindered coordination between teams.
senses.exampleCN: 不同的报表格式妨碍了各团队之间的协调。
senses.why: Coordination needs a clear channel, and hinder narrows it.
senses.whyCN: 协调需要畅通的通道，而这个词把它收窄。

intro.en: Hinder comes from Old English hindrian, to hold back, from hinder, meaning behind. The word is Germanic and has always kept the picture of being placed at the back.
intro.cn: 这个词来自古英语 hindrian「拦在后面」，出自 hinder「在后面」；属日耳曼语，始终保留「被放到后面」的画面。

items.en: The adverb meant behind or in the rear, and it is the same element seen in behind.
items.cn: 这个副词意为「在后面、在后部」，与 behind 中的成分相同。

items.en: The verb meant to keep back or delay, and it was used of people, animals and journeys.
items.cn: 这个动词意为拦阻、耽搁，用于人、牲畜与行程。

items.en: The spelling settled as hinder, and the noun hindrance grew beside it with the same vowel pattern.
items.cn: 拼写后来固定为 hinder，名词 hindrance 以相同的元音模式在旁边长成。

items.en: German hinter and English behind belong to the same Germanic background of rear position.
items.cn: 德语 hinter 与英语 behind 属同一日耳曼语「后位」背景。

items.en: The noun hind, a female deer, is a different word and must not be read into the verb.
items.cn: 名词 hind 指雌鹿，是另一个词，不能读进这个动词里。

items.en: The verb now takes abstract objects such as progress, growth and coordination more often than physical ones.
items.cn: 今天这个动词更多接进展、增长、协调这类抽象宾语，而非具体物。

note.en: The first group looks close or shares the behind root; the second group names neighbouring ideas of obstruction.
note.cn: 第一组与「hinder」形近或共享「在后」词根；第二组是与「阻挡」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for an obstacle or the act of holding something back.
entries.definitionCN: 指障碍物或拦截行为的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective for something that has been held back.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指被拖住的。

entries.definition: The land behind a coast or a settled area, from German hinter.

entries.definition: To block a passage or a process deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 指故意堵塞通道或流程。

entries.definition: To make movement or work awkward, as if by loose equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 指使行动或工作别扭，像是被松散装备缠住。

entries.definition: To limit by rule rather than by obstacle.
entries.definitionCN: 指用规则加以限制，而非用障碍。

entries.definition: To make something happen later than planned.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某事比计划更晚发生。

entries.definition: To reduce speed without necessarily blocking the route.
entries.definitionCN: 指降低速度，未必堵住路线。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the behind root, the old spelling pair behind and hinder, and the false friend hind.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「在后」词根、behind 与 hinder 这对古老拼写伙伴，以及易混的 hind。

normal.en: Hinder begins with the idea of behind, so it is to push something to the back of the queue.
normal.cn: 这个词从「在后面」起步，也就是把某事推到队尾。

normal.en: Behind and hinder share the same Germanic element of rear position.
normal.cn: behind 与 hinder 共享同一日耳曼语「后位」成分。

normal.en: The noun is hindrance, not hinderance, and the vowel changes.
normal.cn: 名词是 hindrance，不是 hinderance，元音有变化。

normal.en: Projects are hindered by missing permits, not by enemies.
normal.cn: 项目是被缺失的许可拖住的，而不是被敌人。

normal.en: Hind, the female deer, is a different word and a common trap.
normal.cn: hind 指雌鹿，是另一个词，也是常见的陷阱。

abstract.en: To hinder is to add distance between a person and the thing they were moving towards.
abstract.cn: 阻碍，就是在人和他要去的地方之间加上距离。

abstract.en: Most obstruction is not a wall but a small stone that makes every step cost more.
abstract.cn: 多数阻碍不是一堵墙，而是一块让每一步都更贵的小石头。

abstract.en: Whatever is put behind schedule was never stopped, only made late.
abstract.cn: 被放到进度后面的东西从未停止，只是被弄晚了。

examples.en: Heavy rain hindered the repair crews for two days.
examples.cn: 大雨使维修队受阻两天。

examples.en: Unclear ownership hindered the transfer of the land.
examples.cn: 权属不清妨碍了这块土地的转让。

examples.en: Lack of sleep hindered his concentration during the test.
examples.cn: 睡眠不足妨碍了他在测试中的专注。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all put an obstacle in a path: a project, movement, growth, attention, a plan, a living thing, a task and coordination.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在一条路径上放置障碍：项目、移动、增长、注意力、计划、生物体、任务与协调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone sits in a narrow path and everyone behind it must edge past sideways.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块落石横在窄路上，后面的人只能侧身挪过去。

branches.en: THE SCHEDULE SLIPS: a project or an economy loses its forward pace.
branches.cn: 进度滑落：项目或经济失去向前的速度。

branches.en: THE PATH IS BLOCKED: a body or a vehicle cannot move freely.
branches.cn: 路径被堵：人或车辆无法自由移动。

branches.en: THE ATTENTION IS CUT: noise or interruption breaks the narrow channel of focus.
branches.cn: 注意力被截断：噪声或打断切断专注这条窄通道。

branches.en: THE DECISION IS STALLED: procedure is used to hold a proposal where it stands.
branches.cn: 决定被卡住：程序被用来把提案按在原处。

branches.en: THE PROCESS UNDERPERFORMS: growth, a task or coordination finishes below its natural level.
branches.cn: 过程发挥不足：生长、任务或协调低于其自然水平。

sensesIntro.cn: hire 表示雇用一个人、租用一件物品，或指被雇用的新员工。

core.en: Paying to bring work or a thing to you.
core.cn: 付钱把劳动或物品请到自己身边。

branches.en: They hired a new driver.
branches.cn: 他们雇了一位新司机。

branches.en: We hired a boat for the afternoon.
branches.cn: 我们租了一条船玩了一下午。

branches.en: The new hire starts on Monday.
branches.cn: 新员工周一开始上班。

branches.en: The person hired is called a hire.
branches.cn: 被雇用的人本身也叫 a hire。

branches.en: The shop hires out bicycles.
branches.cn: 这家店出租自行车。

intro.en: Hire builds hiring, hirer, and hireling.
intro.cn: hire 可构成 hiring、hirer 和 hireling。

latinIntro.en: Hire is Germanic in origin, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: hire 源自日耳曼语，而不是拉丁语。

items.exampleCN: 他们每年夏天雇用学生。
他们重新聘用了老教练。
这里的汽车租赁很便宜。
